'''Aaron James Monroe Francisco''' (born July 5, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|BYU Cougars]] and was signed by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2005.

He was also a member of the [[New York Jets]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Detroit Lions]], and [[Tennessee Titans]].

==Early life==
Aaron James Monroe Francisco was born on July 5, 1983, in [[Lā'ie, Hawai'i]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FranAa20.htm | title=Aaron Francisco | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=25 March 2026}}</ref> He attended [[Kahuku High School]] in [[Kahuku, Hawaii|Kahuku, Hawai'i]] (Oahu), and was an All State and All Oahu Interscholastic Association (OIA) selection as a senior. Francisco helped to lead Kahuku to their first State Championship in 2000.

==College career==
Francisco recorded 88 tackles (43 solo) as a senior in 2004 at [[BYU]]. He finished his career with 330 tackles (167 solo) and seven interceptions and was named first-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] selection as a junior in 2003.

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2005 NFL draft]], Francisco signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on May 2, 2005.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was waived on August 22, 2005.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco signed with the [[New York Jets]] on August 29, 2005.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was waived soon after on September 3, 2005.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad on September 5, 2005.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was promoted to the active roster on October 11.<ref name="Pfr"/> He played in 53 regular season games, starting nine, for the Cardinals from 2005 to 2008.<ref name="Pfr"/> Francisco was famously defending [[Santonio Holmes]] on the Steelers' game winning touchdown in [[Super Bowl XLIII]], a play which made the cover of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.azcentral.com/sports/cardinals/articles/20100202super-bowl-aaron-francisco.html|title=Former Cardinal Aaron Francisco looking for new Super Bowl memory|website=archive.azcentral.com|access-date=2017-01-31}}</ref> Francisco was released by the Cardinals on September 5, 2009.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on September 7, 2009.<ref name="Pfr"/> He appeared in ten games, starting two, for the Colts in 2009.<ref name="Pfr"/> He also played in three playoff games.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco became a free agent after the 2009 season, and signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] on April 12, 2010.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was placed on injured reserve on September 4, and was released on September 8, 2010.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco was signed by the Colts again on October 5, 2010.<ref name="Pfr"/> He played in 12 games, all starts, for Indianapolis during the 2010 season.<ref name="Pfr"/> He also started one playoff game and became a free agent afterwards.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] on August 17, 2011.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released by the Lions on September 3, 2011.<ref name="Pfr"/>

Francisco signed a one-year deal with the [[Tennessee Titans]] on July 24, 2012.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was waived by the Titans on August 31, 2012.<ref name="Pfr"/>

'''Aaron Andrew Merz''' (born August 27, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the seventh round of the [[2006 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2006/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[California Golden Bears football|California Golden Bears]].

==Early life==
Merz attended Wasco High School in [[Wasco, California]] and was a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[High school football|football]], [[basketball]], and [[golf]]. In football, he won All-League honors as both an [[offensive lineman]] and as a [[defensive lineman]].

==College career==
He played [[college football]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he earned a B.A. in sociology in 2005.  Merz joined the [[California Golden Bears football|Golden Bears]] as a walk-on in 2001 and was given a scholarship as reward for his elevated role with the team following the 2003 season.

'''Aaron Halterman''' (born March 31, 1982) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Houston Texans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2005. He played [[college football]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]].

Halterman was also a member of the [[San Diego Chargers]], [[Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Miami Dolphins]]. He earned a [[Super Bowl ring]] as a member of the Colts' [[practice squad]] in [[Super Bowl XLI]].

==Early life==
Halterman attended Center Grove High School in Greenwood, Indiana, and was a letterman in football and track.

==College career==
He started 35 of the 44 games in which he appeared during his four-year collegiate career at Indiana University from 2001 to 2004 under former Dolphins head coach [[Cam Cameron]]. During that time, he totaled 66 receptions for 711 yards and three touchdowns. At Indiana, he majored in [[psychology]].

==Professional career==

===Houston Texans===
Halterman originally went to camp with Houston as an undrafted college free agent in 2005, and spent his entire rookie season on the Texans’ practice squad. He also played with the [[Rhein Fire (NFL Europe)|Rhein Fire]] of [[NFL Europa]] in the spring of 2006, before being waived by the Texans on September 1, 2006.

===Indianapolis Colts===
After brief stints on the practice squads of the [[Miami Dolphins]] and [[San Diego Chargers]] in 2006, Halterman finished the season as a member of the [[Indianapolis Colts]] practice squad, where he spent the final two regular season games and all four playoff contests.

===Miami Dolphins (second stint)===
After his contract expired, Halterman signed with the Miami Dolphins on February 14, 2007,<ref>{{cite web | title=Dolphins sign TE Halterman; OL Pape leaves to Chargers: South Florida Sun-Sentinel | url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/football/pro/dolphins/sfl-0214dolphins%2C0%2C7088657.story?coll=sfla-dolphins-front | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070402233455/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/football/pro/dolphins/sfl-0214dolphins%2C0%2C7088657.story?coll=sfla-dolphins-front | archive-date=April 2, 2007 }}</ref> reuniting him with the Dolphins' head coach Cam Cameron, who mentored him both at Indiana and during his brief tenure with the Chargers.

In August 2008, Halterman was waived/injured with a back injury and subsequently placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]]. An [[exclusive-rights free agent]] in the 2009 offseason, Halterman was non-tendered and became an [[unrestricted free agent]].

==Personal life==
After back injuries prematurely ended Halterman's playing career, he began to pursue a master's degree in counseling and educational psychology with a minor in sports from Indiana University-Bloomington. Halterman took a job as an intern in the guidance office at [[Center Grove High School]] for the 2011–2012 school year as part of his master's program. Halterman graduated with a PhD in counseling psychology from Indiana University-Bloomington in 2019.

'''Aaron Jermaine Ross''' (born September 15, 1982) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He won a [[college football]] national championship in [[2006 Rose Bowl|2005]] with the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and the 2006 [[Jim Thorpe Award]] as the nation's top defensive back. Ross was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the first round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He won [[Super Bowl XLII|Super Bowls XLII]] and [[Super Bowl XLVI|XLVI]] with the Giants.

Ross also played for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], and [[Cleveland Browns]].

==Early life==
{{Citations needed|date=May 2025}}
Ross attended [[John Tyler High School]] in [[Tyler, Texas]], where he competed as quarterback, [[wide receiver]], defensive back and [[running back]] in his three-year career under coach [[Allen Wilson (American football)|Allen Wilson]].  He was named second-team Class 5A All-State after posting six interceptions, three fumble recoveries, three blocked kicks and allowing just one touchdown reception as a senior in 2001.  As a junior, he returned a fumble and a blocked punt for a score, adding 350 rushing yards (on 46 carries) and five touchdowns and caught five passes for 200 yards and two scores that year.  His career-high of 362 all-purpose yards came against [[Katy High School]] in 2001.  Ross also registered three interceptions while rushing for a touchdown against [[Fair Park High School]] that season.  His best game was against [[John Marshall High School (Leon Valley, Texas)|Marshall High School]], when he amassed 272 all-purpose yards, rushed for two touchdowns and had an interception.  As a sophomore, Ross played at [[Fox Tech High School]] in [[San Antonio, Texas]].  There he rushed for 486 yards and nine touchdowns and caught 11 passes for 382 yards and three scores on offense.  He also intercepted five passes and blocked ten kicks.  During his time at both schools, he [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] four times as a [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]] in [[Track and field|track & field]] and twice in [[basketball]].

==College career==
[[File:Aaron Ross.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ross during his tenure with the Texas Longhorns in 2006]]
Ross enrolled at Texas in 2002, but was academically ineligible to play.  He played in thirteen games behind [[Nathan Vasher]] at left cornerback in 2003, coming up with 27 tackles (23 solos), a stop for a loss and two pass break-ups.  He shared right cornerback duties with [[Tarell Brown]] in 2004, appearing in twelve contests.  He recorded 36 tackles (28 solos) with an interception and three pass break-ups.  He also averaged 7.6 yards on 18 punt returns. At the end of the season, he won the first of two [[2005 Rose Bowl|Rose Bowl Championships]]

As a junior, Ross earned All-[[Big 12 Conference]] honorable mention.  He started two games at cornerback and ranked tenth in the nation with a 14.7-yard average on 34 punt returns, returning two for touchdowns.  He also had three interceptions with nine pass break-ups.  He ranked seventh on the team with 62 tackles (35 solos), adding two stops behind the line of scrimmage. He helped the Longhorns to win the [[NCAA Division I FBS National Football Championship|2005 National Championship]].

Finally a full-time starter in 2006, Ross made the most of this opportunity.  He earned [[All-America]]n and All-Big 12 Conference first-team honors, in addition to being named the Thorpe Award winner (nation's top defensive back).  The Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year ranked third on the squad with 80 tackles (59 solos).  He added a sack, two stops for losses and 19 pass deflections.  He caused three fumbles, recovered two and picked off six passes.  He also scored once while averaging 10.4 yards on 23 punt returns.

In 51 games at Texas, Ross started 15 times.  He registered 205 tackles (145 solos) with a one-yard sack, five stops for losses of 21 yards and a quarterback pressure.  He caused three fumbles and recovered two others, returning one for a touchdown.  Ross batted away 33 passes and intercepted ten others for 111 yards in returns (11.1 avg).  He also returned 76 punts for 893 yards (11.8 avg) and three scores, adding 53 yards on a pair of kickoff returns (26.5 avg). He finished his career by winning the 2006 Alamo Bowl and being named the games defensive MVP.

Ross was part of a Texas recruiting class which contained future NFL players [[Rodrique Wright]], [[Justin Blalock]], [[Brian Robison]], [[Kasey Studdard]], [[Lyle Sendlein]], [[David Thomas (American football)|David Thomas]], [[Selvin Young]], and [[Vince Young]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Texas 2002 Football Commitments |publisher=Rivals.com |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/commitlist.asp?Year=2002&School=81&Sport=1 |access-date=January 31, 2008}}</ref>  This class, cited as one of the strongest college recruiting classes ever,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dienhart |first=Tom |year=2002 |title=Ruling class: master recruiter Mack Brown helps Texas consistently bring in top talent, but the Longhorns' 2002 group--led by highly lauded quarterback Vincent Young--might be one of the best recruiting classes ever |publisher=The Sporting News |url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1208/is_6_226/ai_83040183/?tag=content;col1 |access-date=January 31, 2008}}</ref> won the 2005 National Championship.

===New York Giants (first stint)===
[[File:RossWebster.jpg|thumb|Ross and [[Corey Webster]] at training camp in 2010]]
Ross was selected in the first round (20th overall) of the [[2007 NFL draft]] by the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-10 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was one of seven [[Texas Longhorns football|Longhorns]] selected by [[NFL|professional football teams]] in the [[2007 NFL draft]].  The others were [[Michael Griffin (American football)|Michael Griffin]] (number 19 overall), [[Justin Blalock]] (number 39 overall), [[Tim Crowder (football)|Tim Crowder]] (number 56 overall), [[Brian Robison]] (number 102 overall), [[Tarell Brown]] (number 147 overall), [[Kasey Studdard]] (number 183 overall).<ref name="NFL Draft tracker">{{Cite news |date=April 29, 2007 |title=NCAA Schools: TEXAS |publisher=ESPN |url=http://insider.espn.go.com/nfldraft/draft/tracker/school?id=2432&action=login&appRedirect=http%3A%2F%2Finsider.espn.go.com%2Fnfldraft%2Fdraft%2Ftracker%2Fschool%3Fid%3D2432 |access-date=May 1, 2007}}</ref>  [[Lyle Sendlein]] and [[Selvin Young]] were not drafted but signed with NFL teams as free agents.<ref>{{Cite news |title=2007 NFL Draft |publisher=MackBrownTexasFootball |url=http://www.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=40&url_subchannel_id=&url_article_id=2797&change_well_id=2 |url-status=dead |access-date=May 1, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070426101210/http://www.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=40&url_article_id=2797&url_subchannel_id=&change_well_id=2 |archive-date=April 26, 2007}}</ref>

He had first and second career interceptions in week five against the [[New York Jets]], returning his second for his first career touchdown in the same game. As a rookie, Ross recorded 42 tackles, 2.5 tackles for a loss, 1.5 sacks, 9 passes defended and 3 interceptions which he returned a total of 51 yards including a 43-yard touchdown. Later that year, Ross helped the Giants win [[Super Bowl XLII]] by starting at corner, recording 12 tackles, 2 tackles for a loss and a pass defended in the Giants' four playoff games. The team beat the [[New England Patriots]] in that game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ross 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RossAa99/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In his second NFL season in 2008, Ross recorded 52 tackles (4 for loss), 8 passes defended and 3 interceptions (58 return yards including a 50-yard TD).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ross 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RossAa99/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Giants went 12–4 that year, good for the best record in the NFC, but fell to the rivaled [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the divisional round of the [[2008–09 NFL playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 New York Giants Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyg/2008.htm |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Ross missed the first 9 games of the 2009 season due to an injured hamstring. He returned in November to play 4 games before re-injuring the hamstring in mid-December. The Giants, despite being out of the playoff picture, ultimately placed Ross on the injured reserve list on December 31, 2009, just days before the final game of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-12-31 |title=Giants hobble to finish with Jacobs, Ross on IR |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4785186 |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

Just prior to the 2011 campaign, Ross's teammate [[Terrell Thomas]] was placed on injured reserve, which landed Ross the starting job for the season. The Giants would go on to win [[Super Bowl XLVI]] that season against the Patriots again.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XLVI - New York Giants vs. New England Patriots - February 5th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201202050nwe.htm |access-date=December 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed cornerback Ross to a three-year, $15 million contract during the March free agency period in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schefter |first=Adam |last2=Youngmisuk  |first2=Ohm  |date=2012-03-20 |title=Source: Jags, CB Ross agree on a 3-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7712315/jacksonville-jaguars-aaron-ross-agree-3-year-153-million-deal-source-says |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> The transition to Jacksonville was difficult for Ross, who won two Super Bowls in New York, as the Jaguars finished 2–14, tied for the league's worst record.

His brief tenure in Jacksonville saw Ross battling through injuries and struggling in coverage. Ross drew the ire of Jaguars fans by describing his time in Jacksonville as "a nice paid vacation to Florida". He later apologized.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aaron-ross-jacksonville-jaguars-stint-a-vacation-0ap1000000157693|title = Aaron Ross: Jacksonville Jaguars stint a 'vacation'| website=[[NFL.com]] }}</ref>

Ross was released after the start of free agency on March 8, 2013, by newly hired general manager Dave Caldwell.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-03-08 |title=Jaguars let go of safety Landry, corner Ross |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/9030776/dawan-landry-aaron-ross-released-jacksonville-jaguars |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants (second stint)===
Ross signed with the Giants on March 12, 2013, just four days after being released by the Jaguars.<ref>[http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/03/12/aaron-ross-heading-back-to-giants/ Aaron Ross heading back to Giants]</ref>

Ross was placed on injured reserve after week 4 of the 2013 NFL season with a back injury, and his season was over.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants Place Aaron Ross on IR, Activate Will Hill & Make Two Other Moves |url=http://www.sportsmedia101.com/newyorkgiants/2013/10/05/new-york-giants-place-aaron-ross-on-ir-activate-will-hill-make-two-other-moves/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131010153151/http://www.sportsmedia101.com/newyorkgiants/2013/10/05/new-york-giants-place-aaron-ross-on-ir-activate-will-hill-make-two-other-moves/ |archive-date=October 10, 2013}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On June 20, 2014, Ross signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilkening |first=Mike |date=June 20, 2014 |title=Ravens make Aaron Ross signing official, waive three |work=NBCSports.com |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/06/20/ravens-make-aaron-ross-signing-official-waive-three/ |access-date=July 12, 2014}}</ref> On July 24, 2014, Ross tore his Achilles tendon, ending his season.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilkening |first=Mike |date=July 24, 2014 |title=John Harbaugh: Aaron Ross suffers torn Achilles |work=NBCSports.com |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/07/24/john-harbaugh-aaron-ross-suffers-torn-achilles/ |access-date=July 24, 2014}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Ross signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] on August 16, 2015.<ref name="q473">{{cite web | last=Cabot | first=Mary Kay | title=Cleveland Browns sign CB Aaron Ross and LB Everette Brown | website=cleveland.com | date=2015-08-16 | url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/2015/08/cleveland_browns_sign_cb_aaron.html | access-date=2024-12-16}}</ref> He was released by the Browns on August 31, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=August 31, 2015 |title=Browns begin the process of getting to 75 with some vet cuts |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/08/31/browns-begin-the-process-of-getting-to-75-with-some-vet-cuts/ |access-date=September 24, 2015 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref>

As a senior, he was switched to [[cornerback]] and was used on either side of the field. He received [[Western Athletic Conference|All-WAC]] honors, played in the 1975 [[Blue–Gray Football Classic]], the [[Senior Bowl]] and the [[East–West Shrine Game]]. He was the team's best defensive player in his last two years and left as the school's career leader in tackles (275).{{cite web | url=https://gowyo.com/news/2016/6/29/57740b16e4b0bdd131ac7f58_131478088911530985.aspx | title=Wyoming Will Battle Boise State for Second Place Saturday | access-date=April 30, 2022 }} In 2016, he was inducted into the Wyoming Athletics Hall of Fame. ==Professional career== ===Dallas Cowboys=== In the [[1976 NFL draft]], he became only the second [[University of Wyoming|Wyoming]] player ever to be drafted to the [[NFL]] in the first round and the first [[defensive back]] ever to be selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] that high.{{cite web| url=https://gowyo.com/news/2018/4/26/football-congrats-to-wyomings-josh-allen-the-no-pick-in-the-2018-nfl-draft.aspx | title=Congrats to Wyoming’s Josh Allen, the No. 7 Pick in the 2018 NFL Draft | access-date=April 30, 2022}} As a rookie, he was the backup at left cornerback behind [[Benny Barnes]] and was used on passing downs to primarily cover the [[running back]]s. He became a core [[special teams]] player, registering 2 blocked punts. In [[1977 NFL season|1977]], he replaced future hall of famer [[Mel Renfro]] in the starting lineup at right [[cornerback]]. His play was impacted after fracturing the left wrist during a 34-16 win over the [[Washington Redskins]] in the fifth game.{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1144&dat=19771017&id=g3kqAAAAIBAJ&sjid=8FcEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3597,1525876 | title=Doomsday Ruins Redskins | access-date=April 30, 2022}} He missed the last four games of the season because of a heavy cast that was placed on his injured right arm. He returned for the playoffs to help the team win [[Super Bowl XII]], recording three tackles, an [[interception]], a tackle on a run from a punt attempt and a fumble recovery that set up the game-clinching [[touchdown]]. In [[1978 NFL season|1978]], he started all 16 games at cornerback, while making 3 interceptions and 2 fumble recoveries (tied for the team lead). He also had an interception in the playoffs against the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. In [[Super Bowl XIII]], he missed a tackle that allowed [[John Stallworth]] to have a 75-yard [[touchdown]] play.{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=950&dat=19790122&id=qMEwAAAAIBAJ&sjid=3VgDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4756,1595653 | title=Gloomsday For Doomsday | access-date=April 30, 2022}} In [[1979 NFL season|1979]], although he started 16 games, he was limited by bone spurs in his left knee that he developed during [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]]. He intercepted two passes in the season opener against the [[St. Louis Cardinals (NFL)|St. Louis Cardinals]]. In May [[1980 NFL season|1980 season]], he had knee surgery to remove the bone spurs, which led the team to place him in the [[injured reserve list]]. Once the season started, the Cowboys tried to recall him from the [[injured reserve list]], but because they used the procedural recall system to waive him, he was able to be declared as a [[free agent]]. ===Denver Broncos=== On October 14, [[1980 NFL season|1980]], he signed as a [[free-agent]] with the [[Denver Broncos]], playing in 10 games (9 starts) and recording 72 tackles. Kyle played a total of 3 seasons in Denver, starting at [[cornerback|right cornerback]], while leading the team in turnovers in both [[1981 NFL season|1981]] and [[1982 NFL season|1982]], with a total of 5 [[interception]]s and 7 [[fumble]] recoveries. In [[1981 NFL season|1981]], he registered 68 tackles. He retired on April 16, [[1983 NFL season|1983]], after being the Broncos player representative during that season's strike.{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2519&dat=19830407&id=mqpdAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Vl0NAAAAIBAJ&pg=3449,888053 | title=Aaron Kyle Retires | access-date=April 30, 2022}} ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== *[https://wyohof.com/aaron-kyle/?players=aaron-kyle Wyoming Athletics Hall of Fame bio] {{Navboxes|title=|list= {{1976 NFL Draft}} {{Cowboys1976DraftPicks}} {{CowboysFirstPick}} {{Super Bowl XII}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kyle, Aaron}} [[Category:1954 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Players of American football from Detroit]] [[Category:American football cornerbacks]] [[Category:Cass Technical High School alumni]] [[Category:Wyoming Cowboys football players]] [[Category:Dallas Cowboys players]] [[Category:Denver Broncos players]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]]

{{Short description|American politician and football player (born 1984)}} {{Use American English|date=September 2024}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}} {{Infobox officeholder | name = Aaron Rouse | image = Aaron Rouse on First Colonial High School Football Field, Virginia Beach.png | caption = Rouse at [[First Colonial High School]], Virginia Beach | office = Member of the [[Virginia Senate]] | term_start = January 18, 2023 | term_end = | predecessor = [[Jen Kiggans]] | successor = | constituency = [[Virginia's 7th Senate district|7th]] district (2023–2024)

from the at-large district | term_start2 = January 1, 2019 | term_end2 = December 31, 2022 | predecessor2 = Ben Davenport | successor2 = Jennifer Rouse | birth_name = Aaron Roosevelt Rouse | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1984|1|8}} | birth_place = [[Virginia Beach, Virginia|Virginia Beach]], [[Virginia]], U.S. | death_date = | death_place = | spouse = Jennifer | party = [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] | education = [[Virginia Tech]] ([[Bachelor of Science|BS]]) | website = {{URL|rouseforsenate.com|Campaign website}} | module = {{Infobox NFL biography | embed = yes | number = 37, 26 | position = [[Safety (American football position)|Safety]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 4 | weight_lbs = 223 | high_school = [[First Colonial High School|First Colonial]] {{nowrap|(Virginia Beach)}} | college = [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]] | draftyear = 2007 | draftround = 3 | draftpick = 89 | pastteams = * [[Green Bay Packers]] ({{NFL Year|2007|2009}}) * [[New York Giants]] ({{NFL Year|2009}}) * [[Arizona Cardinals]] ({{NFL Year|2010}})* * [[Omaha Nighthawks]] ({{UFL Year|2010}}) * [[Virginia Destroyers]] ({{UFL Year|2011}}–{{UFL Year|2012}}) | highlights = * [[2011 UFL championship game|UFL champion]] ([[2011 UFL championship game|2011]]) * [[UFL championship game]] MVP ([[2011 UFL championship game|2011]]) * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-ACC]] (2005) * Freshman [[All-American]] (2003) | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 143 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] | statvalue2 = 1.0 | statlabel3 = [[Fumble|Forced fumbles]] | statvalue3 = | statlabel4 = [[Pass deflections]] | statvalue4 = 11 | statlabel5 = [[Interceptions]] | statvalue5 = 4 | statlabel6 = [[Touchdown|Defensive touchdowns]] | statvalue6 = 1 | pfr = R/RousAa99}} }} '''Aaron Roosevelt Rouse''' (born January 8, 1984) is an American politician and former professional [[American football|football]] player. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Rouse represents the [[Virginia's 22nd Senate district|22nd district]] in the [[Senate of Virginia]].{{Cite web |title=VPAP: November 8 Elections |url=https://www.vpap.org/electionresults/20230110/state-senate-7/ |access-date=January 11, 2023 |website=The Virginia Public Access Project |language=en}} He previously served on the [[Virginia Beach City Council]]. Rouse played as a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[United Football League (2009–2012)|United Football League]] (UFL). Rouse played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies]] before he was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the third round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. Rouse was also a member of the [[New York Giants]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the NFL and the [[Omaha Nighthawks]] and [[Virginia Destroyers]] of the UFL. From 2019 to 2022, Rouse represented an at-large seat on the [[Virginia Beach, Virginia|Virginia Beach]] city council, having been elected in 2018. He won a [[2023 Virginia's 7th Senate district special election|special election]] to fill the open seat for [[Virginia's 7th Senate district]] in January 2023.{{Cite news |first=Andy |last=Fox |date=January 11, 2023 |title=Democrat Rouse defeats GOP's Adams in 7th District Va. Senate race |url=https://www.wavy.com/news/politics/virginia-politics/democrat-rouse-defeats-gops-adams-in-7th-district-va-senate-race/ |access-date=January 11, 2023 |publisher=[[WAVY-TV]] |language=en-US}} ==Early life== {{unsourced section|date=September 2025}} Rouse attended [[First Colonial High School]] in Virginia where he excelled at many positions, including [[linebacker|outside linebacker]] and [[wide receiver]]. He was named first-team Group AAA by the [[Associated Press]] and second-team by the state coaches as a [[linebacker]]. In his senior year, he was named Defensive Player of the Year in the Virginia Beach District, yet lost the state award to Kai Parham, who also played in the Beach District. He also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[basketball]]. ==College career== Rouse [[redshirted]] his freshman year. At the backup 'Field' outside linebacker position, he finished the season with 46 total tackles (19 solo tackles) with three tackles for losses, one forced fumble and two pass deflections. He was selected to the Freshman All-American team by Rivals.com while appearing in 13 games and starting only one.{{Cite web |title=Packers.com » Team » Players » Aaron Rouse |url=http://www.packers.com/team/players/rouse_aaron/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080415180352/http://www.packers.com/team/players/rouse_aaron/ |archive-date=April 15, 2008 |access-date=April 2, 2008}} During his sophomore season, Rouse remained at his backup position at outside linebacker. He finished the season with 37 total tackles (16 solo tackles) with 2.5 tackles for losses and one forced fumble. At the end of the season, Rouse switched from weak outside linebacker to the defensive backfield at safety. Rouse had an outstanding junior season in 2005 opening at the 'Rover' safety position, collecting 77 total tackles and five interceptions, which prompted him to be named a First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] selection and one of the top safeties in the country.{{Cite news |title=SI.com - 2007 NFL Draft - Aaron Rouse |work=[[SI.com]] |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2007/draft/players/2611.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070509045325/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2007/draft/players/2611.html |archive-date=May 9, 2007}} He was the leader of the Virginia Tech defense and elected to stay in college for his senior season. He had a reputation of hard hits, sometimes resulting in penalties. During the 2006 season, his senior season, Rouse did not perform at the same level; Rouse had an extremely poor performance in the game against [[Georgia Tech]] which landed him on the bench before the end of the game.{{Cite web |url=http://football.about.com/od/playerprofiles/p/aaronrouse.htm |title=Aaron Rouse - Profile of 2007 NFL Draft Prospect Aaron Rouse |access-date=September 12, 2008 |archive-date=October 7, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007154736/http://football.about.com/od/playerprofiles/p/aaronrouse.htm}} He had another disappointing performance the next week against [[Boston College]] which led to him splitting time at the safety position with fellow senior safety, Carey Wade, for a three-week stretch four games before the end of the season. He returned to the starting spot for the final four games of the season, having started ten total games for the season. Rouse finished his senior season with 57 total tackles, one forced fumble, two pass deflections and two interceptions. Rouse finished his college career at Virginia Tech with 217 total tackles (93 solo tackles), 12 tackles for losses, four forced fumbles with one recovery, nine passes defensed and five interceptions. Rouse made 24 starts in 52 career games at Virginia Tech. ==Professional career== ===Pre-draft=== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 4 | weight = 223 | dash = 4.53 | ten split = 1.53 | twenty split = 2.60 | shuttle = 4.19 | cone drill = 6.81 | vertical = 35.0 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 1 | bench = 16 | arm span = 34 3/4 | hand span = 9 3/8 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]/[[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/aaron-rouse/3200524f-5532-0232-8ca9-a37afa8a7570 |title=Aaron Rouse Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |website=NFL.com |access-date=January 6, 2023}}{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=11781&DraftYear=2007 |title=2007 Draft Scout Aaron Rouse, Virginia Tech NFL Draft Scout College Football Profile |access-date=January 6, 2023 |website=draftscout.com}} }} Rouse entered the [[2007 NFL draft]] as one of the top prospects at safety with his unusual combination of size, strength and speed. At 6'4, 223 pounds, he ran 4.59 [[40-yard dash]] at the NFL Combine. While his physical attributes impressed scouts, his lackluster senior season drastically reduced his draft stock; Rouse was projected by many as a late first-round to second-round draft pick. ===Green Bay Packers=== [[File:PackersSecondary-Edit.jpg|thumb|Rouse (middle) with the Green Bay Packers in 2007]] The [[Green Bay Packers]] selected Rouse in the third round (89th overall) of the [[2007 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} On June 8, he signed a four-year, $2.3 million contract with the Packers.{{Cite web |title=Aaron Rouse |url=http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/player_contract.aspx?sport%3DNFl%26id%3D4302 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007102721/http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/player_contract.aspx?sport=NFl&id=4302 |archive-date=October 7, 2008 |access-date=September 12, 2008}} After an injury to starting safety [[Nick Collins]], Rouse made his first NFL start on November 11, during a 34–0 victory over the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. On November 18, Rouse recorded his first interception, when he picked off a [[Vinny Testaverde]] pass on [[Carolina Panthers]]' opening possession in a 31–17 victory over the Panthers. The following week, in a 37–26 win over the [[Detroit Lions]], Rouse recorded his second career interception in just his second career start.{{Cite web |last=Wilde |first=Jason |title=Packers notes: Grant says he'll play Thursday |url=http://www.madison.com/wsj/home/sports//index.php?ntid=257652 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007024345/http://www.madison.com/wsj/home/sports/index.php?ntid=257652 |archive-date=October 7, 2008 |access-date=November 19, 2007}} He was nominated for the week 12 [[Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week|Diet Pepsi Rookie of the Week]] award for his performance against the [[Detroit Lions]] where he made a key game-changing interception against fellow rookie [[Calvin Johnson]]. He finished his rookie campaign with 25 total tackles (22 solo tackles, two assists), four pass deflections and two interceptions while playing in 11 total games, starting in three of them. Rouse helped Green Bay win the 2007 NFC North division championship. The Packers finished the season losing to the New York Giants 23–20 in the NFC championship game, missing out on going to [[Super Bowl XLII]]. Rouse entered the 2008 season as the backup strong safety behind starter [[Atari Bigby]] but an injury to Bigby during the Week 2 matchup at [[Detroit Lions|Detroit]] promoted Rouse to starting strong safety for the Packers' third game of the season against the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and the fourth against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. After sustaining a knee injury in the 4th quarter against Tampa Bay, Rouse was inactive for the Packers' next contest against the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. With Bigby also still out with an injury, Rouse was reinserted into the starting line up for the next two games against the [[Seattle Seahawks]] and the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. Against the Colts, Rouse had seven tackles, two pass defenses, and an interception which he returned 99 yards for a touchdown, tying the longest interception return in Packers history. He was named NFL Defensive player of the week for that performance.{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2008 |title=Aaron Rouse Named NFC Defensive Player Of The Week |url=http://www0.nfl.packers.com/news/releases/2008/10/22/2/?i=2008/10/22/2/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225092714/http://www0.nfl.packers.com/news/releases/2008/10/22/2/?i=2008%2F10%2F22%2F2%2F |archive-date=December 25, 2015 |access-date=September 20, 2012}} After [[Atari Bigby]] returned from injury, Rouse returned to his backup role for the next couple of games until he was injured after his interception in the [[Monday Night Football]] game at [[New Orleans Saints|New Orleans]]. Rouse was inactive for the next contest vs [[Carolina Panthers|Carolina]]. Rouse again entered the season as a backup but started in Week 2 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in place of the injured Atari Bigby. He recorded 9 tackles, 2 assisted, in the game. Rouse was cut by the Packers the following Wednesday, on September 23, 2009, and replaced by [[Matt Giordano]].{{Cite web |title=Packers.com » News » Press Releases » September 23, 2009: Packers Sign S Giordano, Release S Rouse; Sign T Randolph to Practice Squad |url=http://www.packers.com/news/releases/2009/09/23/2/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090926025533/http://www.packers.com/news/releases/2009/09/23/2 |archive-date=September 26, 2009 |access-date=September 23, 2009}} ===Later career=== Rouse was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Giants]] on September 24, 2009, after [[Kenny Phillips]] was placed on [[injured reserve]]. He was released on March 6, 2010.{{cn|date=September 2024}} Rouse signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on August 3, 2010.{{Cite web |url=http://blog.azcardinals.com/2010/08/03/cutting-sheik-highsmith-among-cards-moves/ |title=Cutting Sheik, Highsmith among Cards' moves |access-date=August 3, 2010 |archive-date=September 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100918095244/http://blog.azcardinals.com/2010/08/03/cutting-sheik-highsmith-among-cards-moves/ |url-status=dead}} He was waived on August 18. After being released by the Cardinals, Rouse signed with the [[Omaha Nighthawks]] of the United Football League (UFL) for the 2010 season. Rouse continued with the UFL for the 2011 season, joining the [[Virginia Destroyers]] for the 2011 season. A highlight of Rouse's time with the Destroyers was the [[2011 UFL championship game]], in which Rouse recorded three interceptions en route to a 17–3 win; Rouse was designated the game MVP.{{cn|date=September 2024}} ==Political career== In 2018, Rouse ran for an at-large seat on the Virginia Beach City Council.{{Cite news |last=Minium |first=Harry |date=April 7, 2018 |title=Former Virginia Tech football player Aaron Rouse brings a different vibe to Beach City Council race |work=The Virginian-Pilot |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/sports/columns/article_0b2efd1a-36a2-11e8-81c5-a3d250b01c4e.html |access-date=May 22, 2020}} There were six candidates running for two seats. Rouse got the most votes and was elected alongside incumbent councilman John Moss.{{Cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Stacy |last2=Coutu |first2=Peter |last3=Skelton |first3=Alissa |date=November 6, 2018 |title=In several tight races, most incumbents win re-election for Virginia Beach City Council |work=The Virginian-Pilot |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/government/local/article_dd8caa8c-dc74-11e8-b995-cb1892daf88e.html |access-date=May 22, 2020}} On February 27, 2020, Rouse announced he would run for mayor in the [[2020 Virginia Beach mayoral election|November election]], facing incumbent [[Bobby Dyer (politician)|Bobby Dyer]].{{cite web |last1=Skelton |first1=Alissa |title=Virginia Beach Councilman Aaron Rouse to run for mayor |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/government/local/vp-nw-virginia-beach-mayor-0228-20200228-j7mudumqe5horpb63n6mhzmiu4-story.html |website=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |access-date=October 1, 2020 |date=February 27, 2020}} On May 30, 2020, he announced that he was dropping out of the race citing the [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]] as the reason for ending his campaign.{{cite web |last1=Kennedy |first1=Sean |title=Virginia Beach Councilman Aaron Rouse drops out of mayoral race 2020}} On March 14, 2022, Rouse announced he would be running for the Virginia State Senate in newly formed District 22 in the 2023 election.{{cite news |author=Parker, Stacy |title=Virginia Beach Councilman Aaron Rouse to run for state Senate |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/government/elections/vp-nw-aaron-rouse-senate-0315-20220314-as2sgdgcpfflxlxjzuhyx5ldxa-story.html |website=PilotOnline.com |date=March 14, 2022 |access-date=March 15, 2022}} He was succeeded on the city council by his wife Jennifer Rouse, a [[community college]] instructor.{{cite web|url=https://www.wavy.com/news/local-news/virginia-beach/jennifer-rouse-aaron-rouse-wife-to-run-for-virginia-beach-city-council/|title=Jennifer Rouse, Aaron Rouse's wife, to run for Virginia Beach City Council|last=Ayo|first=Julius|date=April 3, 2022|access-date=July 7, 2025|website=[[WAVY-TV]]}} After [[Jen Kiggans]] was elected to the [[U.S. House of Representatives]], Rouse became a candidate to succeed her in [[Virginia's 7th Senate district]] in the [[2023 Virginia's 7th Senate district special election|January 2023 special election]].{{cite news |title=Rouse, Adams running to fill Va. State Senate seat vacated by Kiggans |url=https://www.wavy.com/news/politics/virginia-politics/virginia-beach-city-councilman-aaron-rouse-to-make-special-announcement-monday/ |publisher=[[WAVY-TV]] |date=November 14, 2022}} Rouse, a Democrat, narrowly defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Kevin H. Adams on January 10, 2023, to become the district's senator-elect, flipping the seat. '''Aaron Gibson''' (born September 27, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Detroit Lions]], [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Chicago Bears]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Wisconsin]]. Gibson holds the record for heaviest NFL player ever. He was listed at 410 lbs by the Cowboys in 2002.<ref name="weight"/>

==Early life==
Gibson attended [[Decatur Central High School]], where he [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[American football|football]] and [[track and field|track]]. He weighed over 350 lbs in high school.<ref name="weight">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-palm-beach-post/173339616/|title=Pressure to grow burdened Gibson |last=Frias |first=Carlos |date=October 29, 2006 |newspaper=Palm Beach Post}}</ref>

He was a two-way player. As a senior, he was a first-team All-state selection and was named as a Top 33 Pick by the Bloomington Herald-Times. As a [[defensive tackle]], he had 8 fumble recoveries and 11 passes defensed.

==College career==
Gibson accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Wisconsin]]. He didn't play in his freshman year because of failing to meet the requirements of [[Proposition 48 (NCAA)|Proposition 48]]. The next year, he was a reserve [[right tackle]] behind [[All-American]] [[Jerry Wunsch]] and was used primarily as a blocking [[tight end]], after making his debut in the fifth game against [[Ohio State University]].<ref name="sportsillustrated"/>

As a junior in 1997, he became the starter at [[right tackle]]. He spent two seasons blocking for [[Heisman Trophy]] winner [[Ron Dayne]], who set the NCAA Division I career rushing
record (6,397 yards) in 1999.

As a senior in 1998, Gibson was recognized as a consensus first-team [[All-American]], after having been named to the first-teams of the Football Writers Association, American Football Coaches Association, and the ''Football News'' and the Walter Camp Foundation. He was also a unanimous first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] selection. He was the first player in school history to be named a finalist for the [[Lombardi Award]] and [[Outland Trophy]] awards.

==Professional career==

===Pre-draft===
In the 1999 [[NFL Scouting Combine]], Gibson ran the [[40-yard dash]] in 5.3 seconds.<ref name="sportsillustrated">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1999/02/22/256260/big-cheese-the-badgers-aaron-gibson-pruned-his-weight-to-371-and-blossomed-into-a-bulldozer-of-a-blocker-who-probably-will-be-the-first-lineman-taken-in-the-nfl-draft |title=Big Cheese The Badgers Aaron Gibson Pruned His Weight To 371 And Blossomed Into A Bulldozer Of A Blocker Who Probably Will Be The First Lineman Taken In The NFL Draft |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=April 1999 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> He was described as "a proto-type right tackle in the NFL," for having "a huge body with big legs and a gigantic chest".<ref name="sportsillustrated"/>

===Detroit Lions===
Gibson was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] with the 27th overall pick in the [[1999 National Football League Draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=March 28, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was expected to be the starting [[right tackle]] as a rookie, but suffered a left shoulder injury in an April post-draft minicamp and was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].

The following season, he started the first 10 games at [[right tackle]], until suffering a right shoulder injury (torn posterior subluxation) and being placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on December 4. In [[2001 Detroit Lions season|2001]], he started five of the first six games of the season, before being waived on October 30.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2001/10/31/lions-waive-99-top-pick-gibson/ | title=Lions waive '99 top pick Gibson | date=October 31, 2001 | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On October 31, 2001, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] but played only in the season finale. In 2002, Gibson had the distinction of becoming the NFL's first player to be officially listed at {{convert|400|lb|kg|0|disp=or}}.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2002/07/28/nfl-lineman-comes-up-big-no-fat-lies/ | title=NFL lineman comes up big: no fat lies | date=July 28, 2002 | access-date=February 19, 2018 | archive-date=September 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930092848/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2002-07-28/sports/0207280330_1_gibson-ted-washington-heaviest-player | url-status=live }}</ref> Gibson was limited by a knee injury in [[training camp]] and eventually released on September 18, 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 19, 2002 |title=Cowboys release Gibson |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=20020919&id=CxZZAAAAIBAJ&sjid=bkYNAAAAIBAJ&pg=5646,4038817&hl=es |access-date=February 19, 2018 |website=The Victoria Advocate|via=Google News}}</ref> He holds the record for heaviest NFL player ever.<ref name="weight"/> He was listed at 410 lbs, by the Cowboys in 2002.<ref name="weight"/>

===Chicago Bears===
On November 26, 2002, he was signed by the [[Chicago Bears]] as a [[free agent]] to replace an injured [[Marc Colombo]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2002/11/27/big-deal-bears-bring-in-gibson/ | title=Big deal: Bears bring in Gibson | access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> In 2003, he had his most consistent professional season, starting at [[right tackle]] in all sixteen games with the Bears, after Colombo was lost for the year when he was placed on the Physically Unable to Perform list. In 2004, he played four games (three starts) and was declared inactive in 10. It would be the last season in which he made an appearance in a regular season NFL game.

===Buffalo Bills===
On April 5, 2006, Gibson signed with the Buffalo Bills as a [[free agent]]. He was cut on August 28.

===Austin Wranglers===
On January 24, [[2007 Arena Football League season|2007]], he was signed by the [[Austin Wranglers]] of the [[Arena Football League]].<ref name="wranglers">{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=104 |title=Aaron Gibson |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On April 4, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]]. On May 5, he was activated. He played in eleven games and had 3 tackles for the season.<ref name="wranglers"/>

===Utah Blaze===
On July 30, 2007, Gibson was traded along with [[defensive line]]man Rob Schroeder to the [[Utah Blaze]] in exchange for past considerations.<ref name="wranglers"/>

===Dallas Desperados===
On October 12, 2007, he was traded to the [[Dallas Desperados]] in exchange for [[offensive line]]man [[Devin Wyman]] and future considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/news/?page=pressrel&article=7971 |title=Blaze trade Gibson to Dallas |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=October 12, 2007|access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On February 22, [[2008 Arena Football League season|2008]], Gibson was released by the Desperados, owned by [[Jerry Jones]], who also owned [[history of the Dallas Cowboys|the Dallas Cowboys]], where Gibson had previously played.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/news/?page=pressrel&article=8334 |title=Desperados release eight, re-sign Jones |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Gladiators===
On March 13, [[2008 Arena Football League season|2008]], he was signed by the [[Cleveland Gladiators]] of the AFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/news/?page=pressrel&article=8478 |title=Gladiators Sign Aaron Gibson |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On May 22, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].

===Bossier-Shreveport Battle Wings===
On March 22, [[2010 Arena Football League season|2010]], he was assigned to the [[Bossier-Shreveport Battle Wings]] of the AFL.<ref name="wings">{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=141 |title=Bossier-Shreveport Battle Wings Team Roster |publisher=ArenaFan.com |date=2014 |access-date=February 19, 2018}}</ref> On August 9, he was suspended by the team.<ref name="wings"/> He was not re-signed after the season.

'''Aaron Brown''' (born October 10, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] and [[return specialist]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the sixth round of the [[2009 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]]. He recorded a 10.45 100-meter dash time on the track, one of the fastest prep times in the nation in 2004.

==College career==
Brown made an immediate impact at [[Texas Christian University]].  In his first game as a [[true freshman]] in 2005, he ran for 163 yards in a nationally televised game against [[Utah Utes|Utah]].  For the year, he rushed for 758 yards and six touchdowns, as well as three receiving touchdowns.  His efforts helped the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|Horned Frogs]] win the [[Mountain West Conference]] championship in their first year as members of the conference, and Brown himself was named [[2005 Mountain West football season|MWC Freshman of the Year]].

As a sophomore in [[2006 TCU Horned Frogs football team|2006]], Brown led TCU with 801 rush yards and nine touchdowns, and was the team's second-leading receiver with 34 receptions for 455 yards and one touchdown.  His 84-yard touchdown reception against [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]] put the Frogs ahead for good in what was their third consecutive victory over teams from the [[Big 12 Conference]].  He was named Second-team All-MWC.

Before his junior year in [[2007 TCU Horned Frogs football team|2007]], Brown was named [[2007 Mountain West football season|Preseason MWC Offensive Player of the Year]].

==Professional career==

===Detroit Lions===
He was selected in the sixth round by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the [[2009 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During his first NFL pre-season game, Brown scored two touchdowns, in the victory against the Atlanta Falcons.

On September 4, 2011, he was waived by the Lions. He was re-signed on November 28 and released again on December 27.

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Brown signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on February 17, 2012.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kirkendall | first=Josh | title=Cincinnati Bengals Sign Former Lions Running Back Aaron Brown | website=Cincy Jungle|publisher=SB Nation | date=2012-02-17 | url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2012/2/17/2806793/cincinnati-bengals-sign-former-lions-running-back-aaron-brown | access-date=2025-06-20}}</ref> He was waived on August 24, 2012.

== Professional career ==
Hayden was drafted by the [[San Diego Chargers]] during the [[1995 NFL draft]] in the fourth round with  the 104th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1995 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1995/draft.htm |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== San Diego Chargers ===
During the 1995 season, Hayden would make his NFL regular season debut in Week 11 against the [[Denver Broncos]]. However, it wouldn't be until Week 14 before getting his first career touchdown in a 31–13 win against the [[Cleveland Browns]]. He would have 2 touchdowns that game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at San Diego Chargers – December 3rd, 1995 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199512030sdg.htm |access-date=February 9, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He would also make a start in the playoffs where the Chargers would lose against the Indianapolis Colts in the wild card round. Hayden would rush 80 yards in 18 carries in the game.

Hayden would return to San Diego for the 1996 season for 11 games, where he would record 55 carries for 166 yards, with no touchdowns.

=== Green Bay Packers ===
For the 1997 season, Hayden was signed by the Green Bay Packers. With Green Bay, he rushed for 148 yards with 32 carries in the regular season, helping the Packer make the playoffs. Throughout the playoffs, Hayden would see little time on the field. The Packers would end up making [[Super Bowl XXXII]], losing 24–31 against the Denver Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl XXXII – Green Bay Packers vs. Denver Broncos – January 25th, 1998 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199801250den.htm |access-date=February 9, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Aaron Michael Maybin''' (born April 6, 1988) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. He was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the first round of the [[2009 NFL draft]], and also played for the [[New York Jets]].

Maybin's professional football career lasted until 2013, after which he became a full-time professional artist. He is also the founder of Project Mayhem, and the author of the 2017 book ''Art Activism''. He is a teacher at Matthew A. Henson Elementary in his hometown of [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]].

==College career==
Maybin attended [[Pennsylvania State University]], where he played for coach [[Joe Paterno]]'s [[Penn State Nittany Lions football]] team from 2006 to 2008.  He [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] during the 2006 season. He had 12 [[Tackle (football move)|tackle]]s, with 4.5 tackles for losses, one forced [[fumble]] and one pass breakup in 2007. He was fourth on the team with four [[Quarterback sack|sack]]s and was named to the ''[[Sporting News]]'' Freshman [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] team.

Maybin had a breakout season in 2008. He was selected as the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Defensive Player of the Week following a six-tackle, two-[[Quarterback sack|sack]] performance in Penn State's 48–7 defeat of [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]], in which he also forced two key fumbles. He was named a Mid-season All-American by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', ''[[College Football News]]'' and [[CBS Sports]].<ref name="midseasonaa">{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2008 |title=Trio of Nittany Lions honored on mid-season All-America teams |url=http://live.psu.edu/story/35380/nw2 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504125014/http://live.psu.edu/story/35380/nw2 |archive-date=May 4, 2009 |access-date=October 18, 2008 |publisher=The Pennsylvania State University}}</ref> At the end of the season, he was named a consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]]<ref name="waltercampaa">{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Mark |date=December 12, 2008 |title=Maybin, Shipley Gain All-America Honors |url=http://pennstate.scout.com/2/820588.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081212193111/http://pennstate.scout.com/2/820588.html |archive-date=December 12, 2008 |access-date=December 12, 2008 |publisher=Fight On State/Scout.com}}</ref><ref name="fwaaaa">{{Cite web |date=December 13, 2008 |title=FWAA Names 2008 All-America Team |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2008/allamerica081213.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081217021436/http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2008/allamerica081213.html |archive-date=December 17, 2008 |access-date=December 13, 2008 |publisher=Football Writers Association of America}}</ref> and a consensus first-team All-Big Ten selection.<ref name="allbigten">{{Cite web |title=2008 All-Big Ten Conference Football Team: As selected by Conference Coaches |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/psu/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2008_AllBigTen.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303180003/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/psu/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2008_AllBigTen.pdf |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |access-date=November 25, 2008 |publisher=GoPSU.com}}</ref>

Maybin was on the 2008 [[Walter Camp Award]] watchlist<ref name="wc watchlist">{{Cite web |date=November 13, 2008 |title=Maybin on Watch Lists for Walter Camp Player of the Year and Hendricks Defensive End Award |url=http://gopsusports.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/111308aac.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130121054853/http://gopsusports.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/111308aac.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 21, 2013 |access-date=November 14, 2008 |publisher=Penn State Intercollegiate Athletics}}</ref> and was one of three finalists for the 2008 [[Ted Hendricks Award|Ted Hendricks]]<ref name="Hendricks">{{Cite news |date=December 2, 2008 |title=Penn State's Maybin is Hendricks finalist |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/s_601133.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504054659/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/s_601133.html |archive-date=May 4, 2009 |access-date=December 3, 2008 |work=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review}}</ref> and [[Chuck Bednarik Award|Chuck Bednarik]] awards, awarded annually to collegiate football's top defensive end and defensive players, respectively.<ref name="maxwellfinalist">{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Mark |date=November 24, 2008 |title=Maybin a Bednarik Finalist |url=http://pennstate.scout.com/2/815283.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081224111433/http://pennstate.scout.com/2/815283.html |archive-date=December 24, 2008 |access-date=November 26, 2008 |publisher=Fight On State}}</ref> He was named [[the Pigskin Club of Washington, D.C.]] National Defensive Player of the Year.<ref name="dcpigskin">{{Cite news |last=Jones |first=Ryan |date=March–April 2009 |title=What Off-Season? |work=The Penn Stater |page=25}}</ref>

After that the Jets went on to win the game 34–19.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Maese |first=Rick |date=December 5, 2011 |title=Stats, scores and schedules |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/post/aaron-maybin-comes-up-with-key-sack/2011/12/04/gIQAVOPCUO_blog.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106072944/https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/post/aaron-maybin-comes-up-with-key-sack/2011/12/04/gIQAVOPCUO_blog.html |archive-date=January 6, 2018 |access-date=August 23, 2017 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> Maybin's ability to get to the quarterback made it difficult for some offensive linemen to contain him, resulting in his team-leading 6 sacks in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 New York Jets Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyj/2011.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220102184700/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyj/2011.htm |archive-date=January 2, 2022 |access-date=January 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |publisher=Sports Reference, LLC.}}</ref>

'''Aaron Geddes Graham''' (born May 22, 1973)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Graham Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GrahAa20.htm |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (American football)|center]] who played six seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] (1996–1999), the [[Oakland Raiders]] (2001), and the [[Tennessee Titans]] (2002). Graham also played college football for the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] from 1991 to 1995, where he played in three national championship games, winning two in 1994 and 1995.

== Early life ==
Graham attended [[Denton High School]] in Denton, Texas, where he played for the Denton Broncos high school football team.

== College career ==
Graham attended the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, where he played college football for the Nebraska Cornhuskers from 1991 to 1995 under head coach [[Tom Osborne]]. Graham played as the starting center for most of the 1993 through 1995 seasons, and played in three national championship games, winning two back-to-back in 1994 and 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dataomaha.com/huskers/player/2606/aaron-graham|title=Aaron Graham - Class of 1992 - Nebraska football recruits|website=dataomaha.com|language=en|access-date=August 5, 2019|archive-date=August 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190805172453/https://dataomaha.com/huskers/player/2606/aaron-graham|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his 1993 season, Graham and the Cornhuskers entered the [[1994 Orange Bowl]] ranked number 2 at 11-0 but lost to [[Florida State University]]. In 1994, Graham and the Cornhuskers finished the season with an 13–0 record, beating Miami for the national title in the [[1995 Orange Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.footballstudyhall.com/2017/6/28/15887246/1995-orange-bowl-nebraska-miami-tom-osborne|title=1994: Nebraska 24, Miami 17|last=C|first=Bill|date=June 28, 2017|website=Football Study Hall|access-date=August 5, 2019}}</ref> In his senior season, Graham and the Cornhuskers won the rest of their regular season games, finishing 12–0. Nebraska won the championship game against Florida in the Fiesta Bowl, 62–24.

As a senior, Graham was named the 1995 AP All-American Football Player. He won multiple awards during his college career such as Academic All-American from 1994 to 1995 and the 1996 Top Eight Award that is given to the nation's elite scholar athletes.  While playing [[college football]] for [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]] he was also recognized by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] for "athletic accomplishments, academic achievements, character, leadership and other activities".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1933&dat=19960109&id=btcgAAAAIBAJ&sjid=DmsFAAAAIBAJ&pg=1467,598867&hl=en|title=NCAA honors Graham|date=January 9, 1996|work=[[McCook Daily Gazette]]|access-date=February 18, 2016|publisher=[[Associated Press|AP]]|page=9}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Graham was selected by Arizona in the fourth round of the 1996 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1996 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1996/draft.htm |access-date=March 30, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Graham played six seasons as center in the NFL with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] (1996–1999), the [[Oakland Raiders]] (2001), and the [[Tennessee Titans]] (2002). Graham was planning on going back for his 7th season with the [[Tennessee Titans]], but instead retired after six seasons with the NFL.

'''Aaron Templeton Mitchell, Jr.''' (born December 15, 1956) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[UNLV Rebels football|UNLV Rebels]].

==Early life==
Mitchell attended [[North Hollywood High School]], before moving on to [[College of the Canyons]] for two years.

He transferred to the [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas]], where he was the starter at right [[cornerback]] for the following two years. As a senior, he registered 6 interceptions and 12 passes defensed.

In 1989, he was inducted into the [[University of Nevada, Las Vegas|UNLV]] Athletics Hall of Fame.

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
The [[Dallas Cowboys]] liked Mitchell's athletic ability and selected him in the second round (55th overall) of the [[1979 NFL draft]]. In [[1980 NFL season|1980]], he became the starter at right [[cornerback]], replacing [[Aaron Kyle]] and recording 3 interceptions.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=19730928&id=wwJPAAAAIBAJ&sjid=FwIEAAAAIBAJ&pg=7292,853163 | title=Theft By Harper Keys Woodward Over Start | accessdate=February 19, 2016}}</ref> In [[1981 NFL season|1981]], he was passed on the depth chart by [[Dennis Thurman]] and was traded to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in exchange for an eleventh draft choice (#295-George Thompson).<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=888&dat=19820105&id=5p9IAAAAIBAJ&sjid=RHsDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6109,3854719 | title=Looking Ahead | accessdate=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
The Buccaneers moved him to [[free safety]] to take advantage of his aggressive hitting and to limit his exposure in coverage. He was placed on [[injured reserve list]] for the last two games of the season, after suffering a collapsed lung.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1454&dat=19811213&id=kNdOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=VhMEAAAAIBAJ&pg=4950,2924478&hl=es | title=Tampa's Mitchell Sidelined | accessdate=February 19, 2016}}</ref> He was released before the start of the [[1982 NFL season|1982 season]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1356&dat=19820824&id=qr9PAAAAIBAJ&sjid=2QUEAAAAIBAJ&pg=2255,4207761&hl=es | title=Tampa Bay Waives Six | accessdate=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

===Arizona Wranglers===
In [[1983 USFL season|1983]], he signed with the [[Arizona Wranglers]] of the [[United States Football League|USFL]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=892&dat=19820917&id=P69OAAAAIBAJ&sjid=qkwDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4406,586976 | title=Wranglers sign Ex-Cowboy | accessdate=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Express===
In [[1984 USFL season|1984]], he played with the [[Los Angeles Express (USFL)|Los Angeles Express]] of the [[United States Football League|USFL]], until announcing his retirement in [[1985 USFL season|1985]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1320&dat=19850124&id=2jxWAAAAIBAJ&sjid=qukDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3690,2998891 | title=Transactions | accessdate=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is currently a financial adviser.
