===Kansas City Chiefs===
Murray was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the fifth round (163rd overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  On September 3, 2016, Murray was released by the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Down to NFL Mandated Roster Limit|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Down-to-NFL-Mandated-Roster-Limit/eaa26747-962f-4a0c-a143-502c64f318ed|website=Chiefs.com|access-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013185227/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Down-to-NFL-Mandated-Roster-Limit/eaa26747-962f-4a0c-a143-502c64f318ed|archive-date=October 13, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Arizona Cardinals ===
On September 4, 2016, Murray was signed by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] to their practice squad. On September 12, 2016, Murray was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Cardinals sign QBs Aaron Murray and Zac Dysert|url=http://arizonasports.com/story/818979/matt-barkley-bears-practice-squad-roster-cardinals-sign-aaron-murray/|website=arizonasports.com|date=September 4, 2016}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia Eagles ===
On September 13, 2016, Murray was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] to their practice squad reuniting him with former Chief offensive coordinator and Eagle head coach [[Doug Pederson]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles sign former Kansas City Chiefs QB Aaron Murray to practice squad|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/sports/eagles/Eagles-sign-former-Kansas-City-Chiefs-aaron-murray.html|website=Philly.com|date=September 13, 2016 }}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Rams ===
On March 23, 2017, Murray was signed by the [[Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Agree to Terms with QB Aaron Murray|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Agree-to-Terms-with-QB-Aaron-Murray/3a189d3c-73cb-4ac4-aed1-5ee306668bdc|author=Simmons|website=TheRams.com|date=March 23, 2017|access-date=March 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324174351/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Agree-to-Terms-with-QB-Aaron-Murray/3a189d3c-73cb-4ac4-aed1-5ee306668bdc|archive-date=March 24, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 11, 2017, he was waived by the Rams.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rams waive quarterback Aaron Murray|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/la-sp-rams-aaron-murray-waive-20170511-story.html|author=Klein, Gary|work=Los Angeles Times |date=May 11, 2017}}</ref>

===Atlanta Legends===
In 2018, Murray signed with the [[Atlanta Legends]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] for the 2019 season. Murray was protected by the Legends on November 27, 2018, for the [[2019 AAF QB Draft]], where he was selected second overall.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wilson|first=Ryan|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/alliance-of-american-football-qb-draft-aaron-murray-christian-hackenberg-highlight-qbs-taken/|title=Alliance of American Football QB Draft: Aaron Murray, Christian Hackenberg highlight QBs taken|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=November 27, 2018|access-date=November 27, 2018}}</ref>

Murray began the [[2019 AAF season]] as the backup to [[Matt Simms (American football)|Matt Simms]]. In the fourth game against the [[Arizona Hotshots]], Murray relieved an injured Simms in the first quarter and led the Legends to a 14–11 victory, the first win in team history; he completed 20 of 33 passes for 254 yards and led the team in rushing with 54 yards on seven carries.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/football/aaron-murray-takes-over-quarterback-for-atlanta-legends/3GsLor6aTruKWIXNF20jeP/|title=Aaron Murray takes over at quarterback, leads Atlanta Legends to first win|newspaper=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=March 3, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2019}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rothstein |first1=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Vipers===
Murray was allocated as one of the "Tier 1" quarterbacks in the [[2020 XFL draft]] on October 15, 2019, assigned to the [[Tampa Bay Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Florio|first=Mike|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/10/15/xfl-announces-its-eight-allocated-quarterbacks/|title=XFL announces its eight allocated quarterbacks|publisher=[[Profootballtalk.com]]|date=October 15, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2019}}</ref> Murray signed a contract with the team on November 4, 2019. In his debut game and only start for the Vipers, Murray completed 16 of 34 pass attempts for 231 yards with zero touchdowns and two interceptions. He suffered a foot injury and missed the week 2 game.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Austin |first1=Brooks |title=Aaron Murray Ruled Out For Week 2 of XFL |url=https://www.si.com/college/georgia/news/aaron-murray-ruled-out-week-2-xfl |access-date=February 18, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=February 14, 2020}}</ref>

[[Taylor Cornelius]] started the final four games for the Vipers.

He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==

'''Aaron Pettrey''' (born June 17, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[placekicker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]].<ref>Boyles, Bob & Paul Guido. ''The USA Today College Football Encyclopedia.'' Skyhorse, 2009. 809.</ref><ref>Boyles, Bob & Paul Guido. ''50 Years of College Football: A Modern History of America's Most Colorful Sport.'' Skyhorse, 2007. 1085.</ref> Pettrey was signed to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]' roster on November 16, 2010, after a season-ending injury to [[Mike Nugent]], another former Buckeye. Pettrey was waived by the Bengals on November 30, 2010. He was two for four on field goal attempts in two games.

==Early life==
Pettrey attended Raceland–Worthington High School and served as [[quarterback]] and placekicker. In a September 26, 2003, game at [[Berea, Kentucky|Berea]],<ref name=Raceland03>{{cite web| url=http://scoreboard.12dt.com/scoreboard/khsaa/kyfb3/?id=15335 |title=Raceland 2003 Kentucky High School Football |work=[[Kentucky High School Athletic Association]] |accessdate=September 14, 2013}}</ref> Pettrey kicked a Kentucky state-record 58-yard [[Field goal (American and Canadian football)|field goal]].<ref name=Records>{{cite web |url=http://khsaa.org/records/football/individualrecords.pdf |title=KHSAA Football Record Book - Individual Records |work=[[Kentucky High School Athletic Association]] |accessdate=September 14, 2013}}</ref> This broke [[Middlesboro High School|Middlesboro]]'s Dustin Wynn's record of 57 yards,<ref name=Records/> set on October 2, 1998, at [[Harlan, Kentucky|Harlan]].<ref name=Middlesboro98>{{cite web| url=http://scoreboard.12dt.com/scoreboard/riherds/kyfb/4286 |title=Middlesboro 1998 Kentucky High School Football |work=[[Kentucky High School Athletic Association]] |accessdate=September 14, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
Pettrey attended [[Ohio State University]].
During Pettrey's time at Ohio State, the Buckeyes played in two BCS National Championship Games in 2007 and 2008, won four Big 10 titles, and won a Rose Bowl Championship in 2010.

The 6–1, 202-pound Pettrey was 29-of-39 on field goal attempts during his Ohio State career, with a career-long of 54 yards. Pettrey also connected on 86-of-90 extra point attempts. A strong-legged kicker, Pettrey was 18-of-23 on field goal attempts over 40 yards, and delivered 56 career touchbacks as the Buckeyes' kickoff specialist in 2006 and 2008. (Pettrey was slowed by a hip flexor in '07)

In his final season in 2009, Pettrey handled all of the kicking duties, and was 14-of-20 on field goal attempts and 30-of-31 on extra points during a regular season that was cut short by a torn right MCL. Pettrey recovered quickly enough to kick for the Buckeyes in the Rose Bowl, converting from 45 yards out in the 26–17 win over Oregon.

==Professional career==

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Pettrey kicked for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] for two weeks, making 2 of 4 field goal attempts and converting all 5 PATs attempted.

===Las Vegas Locomotives===
Pettrey kicked for the [[Las Vegas Locomotives]] of the [[United Football League (2009-2012)|United Football League]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.reviewjournal.com/solid-guys-pettrey-coutu-vie-locomotives-kicking-job |title='Solid guys' Pettrey, Coutu vie for Locomotives' kicking job |date=September 8, 2011 |author=Steve Carp |publisher=Stephens Media LLC |work=www.reviewjournal.com |accessdate=July 12, 2013}}</ref> After a 3 for 3 kicking performance in week one, Pettrey was named the UFL's Special Teams Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4296599 |title=OurSports Central Names UFL Players of the Week |author=Fran  |date=September 19, 2011 |publisher=OurSports Central |work=www.oursportscentral.com |accessdate=July 12, 2013}}</ref>

===Cleveland Gladiators===

====2012 season====
Pettrey kicked for the [[Cleveland Gladiators]] of the [[Arena Football League]] in 2012.

====2013 season====
With the Gladiators having kicking problems in 2013, Pettrey was assigned to the Gladiators and solidified the position. He was placed on injury reserve on July 11, 2013.

====2014 season====
Pettrey had his most successful season to date for the Gladiators, making a career high 8 field goals and 106 PATs.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cleveland.com/gladiators/index.ssf/2014/08/former_ohio_state_kicker_kicke.html |title=Former Ohio State kicker kicker Aaron Pettrey is money in the bank for Cleveland Gladiators |author=Tim Warsinskey |date=August 7, 2014 |publisher=Northeast Ohio Media Group LLC. |work=www.cleveland.com |accessdate=August 7, 2014}}</ref> He made 3 game-winning field goals,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cleveland.com/gladiators/index.ssf/2014/08/2014_cleveland_gladiators_brea.html |title=2014 Cleveland Gladiators: Breaking down six wild, last-minute victories |author=Tim Warsinskey |date=August 7, 2014 |publisher=Northeast Ohio Media Group LLC. |work=www.cleveland.com |accessdate=August 7, 2014}}</ref> including a 36-yard shot against the [[Philadelphia Soul]] as time expired to advance to the American Conference Championship.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cleveland.com/gladiators/index.ssf/2014/08/cleveland_gladiators_edge_phil.html#incart_river |title=Cleveland Gladiators edge Philadelphia Soul 39-37 in thrilling Arena Football League playoff game |author=Marc Bona |date=August 2, 2014 |publisher=Northeast Ohio Media Group LLC. |work=www.cleveland.com |accessdate=August 7, 2014}}</ref>
Pettrey helped the Gladiators reach Arena Bowl XXVII.

On September 29, 2014, Pettrey was placed on reassignment by the Gladiators.

====2017 season====
On June 14, 2017, Pettrey was assigned to the Gladiators.

'''Aaron Lavarias''' (born April 27, 1988) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He had previously played for the [[New England Patriots]].

==College career==
He played [[college football]] at [[Idaho Vandals|University of Idaho]].

==Professional career==

===New England Patriots===
On July 27, 2011, he signed as an undrafted [[free agent]]. On September 3, 2011, he was released. On September 5, 2011, he was signed to the Patriots practice squad. On September 14, 2011, he was released. On December 28, 2011, he was signed to the practice squad.  On February 7, 2012, he signed a future contract with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patriots.com/team/roster/Aaron-Lavarias/dcb48c01-eaaf-46b4-9758-4566fd281644 |title=New England Patriots: Aaron Lavarias |accessdate=2012-07-16 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120728082446/http://www.patriots.com/team/roster/Aaron-Lavarias/dcb48c01-eaaf-46b4-9758-4566fd281644 |archivedate=2012-07-28 }}</ref>
Lavarias was released by the Patriots on August 31, 2012 during final cuts.

===Montreal Alouettes===
On October 3, 2012 Lavarias signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League|CFL]]. In his first two seasons, he has recorded 78 tackles with 11 sacks and 1 fumble recovery. On January 2, 2015 Lavarias re-signed a 2-year contract with the [[Montreal Alouettes]].

'''Aaron Mellette''' (born December 28, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the seventh round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Elon University|Elon]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/players/aaron-mellette/ |title=Aaron Mellette|website=nfl.com}}</ref>

==Early life==
Mellette attended [[Southern Lee High School]] in [[Sanford, North Carolina]]. He helped his school to a pair of playoff berths, including a second-round appearance in 2007. He hauled in 1,900 receiving yards and 29 scores in his final two prep seasons, and collected 800 yards and five scores in two years as a return specialist. He was a two-time first-team all-conference pick, and a two-time offensive team MVP.

==College career==
Mellette attended [[Elon University]] from 2008 to 2012. After redshirting in 2008, he notched time in all 12 games as a red-shirt freshman, catching eight balls for 117 yards and two touchdowns.
In 2010, he led the team with 86 catches, 1,100 receiving yards and 12 touchdown receptions, and was ranked third nationally with 7.82 receptions per game and sixth in the nation with 100.0 receiving yards per outing. He posted six 100-plus yard receiving games in 11 outings, and earned first-team all-conference, and second-team All-American honors. In 2011, he earned first-team all-conference, and first-team all-American honours after he led FCS in both receptions per game (10.27) and receiving yards per game (149.0). He set a new Elon and [[Southern Conference|SoCon]] record with 1,639 receiving yards, and finished the year with 113 receptions and averaged 14.5 yards per catch, while finding the end zone 12 times after receptions. He had nine 100-yard receiving games and twice eclipsed the 200-yard mark. In his final season, he amazed with a league-leading 108 points and 18 receiving touchdowns. The TD catches are tied for the second-most ever in a single season in [[Southern Conference|SoCon]] history. He caught 97 passes for 1,398 yards and led the SoCon and ranked second nationally in both receptions per game (8.82) and receiving yards per game (127.09), and eclipsed 100 receiving yards in eight of Elon's 11 contests. He earned all-conference and all-American honours for the third consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web | title=Mellette Repeats as Walter Camp All-American | website=Elon University Athletics | date=2012-12-19 | url=https://elonphoenix.com/news/2012/12/19/FB_1219120834.aspx | access-date=2025-03-13}}</ref>

For his career in the maroon and gold, Mellette posted 4,254 receiving yards, 304 receptions, 44 touchdown catches and 23 100-yard games.  All of those numbers rank second in both Elon and Southern Conference history.

==Professional career==
Mellette was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the seventh round (238th overall) of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=April 27, 2013 |title=Seventh round: Ravens draft WR Aaron Mellette, CB Marc Anthony |work=The Baltimore Sun |url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-ravens-draft-elon-wr-aaron-mellette-in-seventh-round-20130427,0,2220810.story |access-date=October 12, 2022 |archive-date=July 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130702020738/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-ravens-draft-elon-wr-aaron-mellette-in-seventh-round-20130427,0,2220810.story |url-status=dead }}</ref> On June 17, 2014, the Ravens waived Mellette.

'''Aaron Charles Donald'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DonaAa00.htm |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> (born May 23, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 10 seasons with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] franchise. He is considered one of the greatest defensive players of all time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gagnon |first=Brad |date=June 10, 2021 |title=Could Aaron Donald Be the Greatest Defensive Player in NFL History? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2944366-could-aaron-donald-be-the-greatest-defensive-player-in-nfl-history |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=September 5, 2021 |title=Damien Harris calls Aaron Donald the best defensive player of all time |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2021/09/05/rams-nfl-aaron-donald-damien-harris-best-player/ |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Baldinger |first=Brian |author-link=Brian Baldinger |date=June 17, 2019 |title=Why Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald is the greatest interior defensive lineman of all time |url=https://www.nfl.com/videos/why-los-angeles-rams-defensive-tackle-aaron-donald-is-the-greatest-interi-436333 |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

Donald played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]], winning the [[Bronko Nagurski Trophy|Bronko Nagurski]], [[Outland Trophy|Outland]], and [[Bill Willis Trophy|Bill Willis]] trophies along with the [[Chuck Bednarik Award|Chuck Bednarik]] and [[Lombardi Award|Lombardi]] awards in 2013. He was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in the first round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. Donald was named [[Associated Press NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year]] a record three times, along with receiving [[Pro Bowl]] selections in all 10 of his seasons and eight first-team [[All-Pro]] honors. He was also a member of the team that won [[Super Bowl LVI]].

==Early life==
Aaron Charles Donald was born in [[Pittsburgh]], Pennsylvania, on May 23, 1991. He grew up as one of three children in a working-class family in the city's [[Lincoln–Lemington–Belmar (Pittsburgh)|Lincoln–Lemington–Belmar]] neighborhood; Donald later admitted that he was "lazy as a kid." Seeking to provide a sense of structure in his son's life, Donald's father introduced him to workouts, and they would wake up at 4:30 a.m. and workout for nearly two hours in the gym that his father installed in their basement by the time Donald was 12.<ref name="Gonzalez">{{Cite web |last=Gonzalez |first=Alden |date=January 12, 2019 |title=How Rams DT Aaron Donald became the NFL's most unstoppable force |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles-rams/post/_/id/39627/how-rams-dt-aaron-donald-became-the-nfls-most-unstoppable-force |access-date=January 12, 2019 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Donald attended [[Penn Hills High School]], where he played [[high school football]] for head coach Ron Graham.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Divittorio |first=Michael |title=Penn Hills cherishes Aaron Donald as he prepares for Super Bowl debut |url=https://triblive.com/sports/nfl/14566877-74/penn-hills-cherishes-aaron-donald-as-he-prepares-for-super-bowl-debut |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=triblive.com|date=February 2019 }}</ref> Donald was a first-team All-State Class AAAA selection in each of his final two seasons, and compiled 63 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], 15 [[tackles for loss]], and 11 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] as a senior. Donald also started at [[offensive guard]].

Considered a three-star prospect by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Donald was rated as the 37th best [[defensive tackle]] in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald, 2010 Defensive Tackle |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2010/aaron-donald-16845 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20230320184931/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2010/aaron-donald-16845 |archive-date=March 20, 2023 |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He committed to hometown [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh]] over other scholarship offers from [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo]], [[Akron Zips football|Akron]], and [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald Recruit Interests |url=https://247sports.com/Recruitment/Aaron-Donald-3193/RecruitInterests/ |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=247sports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouchette |first=Ed |date=January 29, 2019 |title=Dave Wannstedt and Pitt didn't know what they had in Aaron Donald. Then camp began. |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2019/01/29/aaron-donald-rams-patriots-super-bowl-dave-wannstedt-pitt/stories/201901290088 |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Aaron Donald 2013.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Donald in 2013]]
As a [[true freshman]] in 2010, Donald played in all 13 games as a reserve [[defensive end]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. He recorded 11 tackles, including three for loss, and two sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-donald-1/gamelog/2010 |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2011, Donald moved into the starting lineup and turned in a breakout campaign. He recorded 47 tackles, including 16 for loss, 11 sacks, and a forced [[fumble]] while being named a second-team All-[[Big East Conference (1979–2013)|Big East Conference]] selection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-donald-1/gamelog/2011 |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> 

As a junior in 2012, Donald recorded 64 tackles, including 18.5 for loss, 5.5 sacks, and a forced fumble, earning first-team All-Big East honors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-donald-1/gamelog/2012 |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a senior in 2013, Donald became one of the most productive defensive players in the entire [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]]. He posted 59 tackles, including a career best 28.5 for loss, 11 sacks, and four forced fumbles. Donald was named the [[ACC Defensive Player of the Year]] and was a [[unanimous All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-donald-1/gamelog/2013 |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2013 |title=Aaron Donald named ACC Defensive Player of the Year |url=http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120413aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305132951/http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120413aaa.html |archive-date=March 5, 2016 |access-date=January 17, 2014 |website=www.pittsburghpanthers.com}}</ref>

The University of Pittsburgh retired Donald's {{abbr|No.|Number}} 97 jersey at halftime on November 15, 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |agency=Associated Press |date=September 22, 2025 |title=Aaron Donald to become 11th Pitt player to have number retired |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/46346590/aaron-donald-become-11th-pitt-player-number-retired |access-date=January 19, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Two months later, on January 14, 2026, he was inducted into the [[College Football Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web | title=NFF Announces All-Star 2026 College Football Hall of Fame Class | website=National Football Foundation | date=January 14, 2026 | url=https://footballfoundation.org/news/2026/1/14/nff-announces-all-star-2026-college-football-hall-of-fame-class.aspx | access-date=February 10, 2026}}</ref>

===2014===
{{See also|2014 St. Louis Rams season}}
Donald was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in the first round (13th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=May 9, 2014 |title=Rams add Aaron Donald to their first-round haul |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/rams-add-aaron-donald-to-their-first-round-haul |access-date=February 22, 2026 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> On June 16, 2014, the Rams signed him to a four-year, fully guaranteed $10.13 million rookie contract with a $5.69 million signing bonus and a fifth-year option.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Sportrac.com:Aaron Donald contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/los-angeles-rams/aaron-donald-14422/ |access-date=October 28, 2016 |website=Sportrac.com}}</ref>

Donald made his regular season debut during the season-opening 34–6 loss to the [[Minnesota Vikings]] and finished with four solo tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at St. Louis Rams – September 7th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409070ram.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Donald recorded two tackles and his first NFL sack on [[Josh McCown]] during the narrow 19–17 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – September 14th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409140tam.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 6 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on [[Monday Night Football|''Monday Night Football'']], Donald was given his first career start and finished the 31–17 loss with four solo tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at St. Louis Rams – October 13th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410130ram.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], Donald had five combined tackles and a sack during the narrow 28–26 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at St. Louis Rams - October 19th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410190ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], he recorded two solo tackles and a forced fumble in the 34–7 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Kansas City Chiefs - October 26th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410260kan.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 9 13–10 road victory over the 49ers, Donald recorded two tackles and sacked [[Colin Kaepernick]] once.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at San Francisco 49ers - November 2nd, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411020sfo.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> From Weeks 11–15, he recorded a sack in each game and had a pass deflection in the Week 13 52–0 shutout victory over the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2014 Stats per Game - NFL |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/16716/aaron-donald |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> In the regular season finale against the Seahawks, Donald had a season-high seven combined tackles and strip-sacked [[Russell Wilson]] once during the 20–6 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Seattle Seahawks - December 28th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412280sea.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Donald finished his rookie year with 47 combined tackles (37 solo), nine sacks, two forced fumbles, and a pass deflection in 16 games and 12 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DonaAa00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Donald was one of five rookies selected to the [[2015 Pro Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/probowl.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He won the NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year award and was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=January 31, 2015 |title=Aaron Donald nets Defensive Rookie of the Year honors |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000466462/article/aaron-donald-nets-defensive-rookie-of-the-year-honors?campaign=twitter_atn |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208051132/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000466462/article/aaron-donald-nets-defensive-rookie-of-the-year-honors?campaign=twitter_atn |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 8, 2015 |access-date=July 31, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2014.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2015===
{{See also|2015 St. Louis Rams season}}[[File:AaronDonald99.jpg|thumb|Donald in 2015]]Donald began the 2015 season as a starting defensive tackle. During the season opener against the Seahawks, he finished with nine tackles and two sacks in the 34–31 overtime victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at St. Louis Rams – September 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509130ram.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Donald was named NFC Defensive Player of the Week for the first time after his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 16, 2015 |title=Aaron Donald is 2015's first NFC defensive player of the week |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/09/16/aaron-donald-is-2015s-first-nfc-defensive-player-of-the-week/ |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Washington Redskins]], Donald had five tackles and 0.5 sacks during the 24–10 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Washington Redskins - September 20th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509200was.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], he recorded four tackles and a sack in the 12–6 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at St. Louis Rams - September 27th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509270ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 7 24–6 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]], Donald had three solo tackles and a sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at St. Louis Rams - October 25th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510250ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[Chicago Bears]], he recorded seven tackles, 1.5 sacks, and a fumble recovery in the 37–13 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at St. Louis Rams - November 15th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511150ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Donald had a season-high nine tackles and sacked [[Joe Flacco]] once during the 16–13 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at Baltimore Ravens - November 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220rav.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 13 against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], Donald recorded seven tackles and a sack in the 27–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arizona Cardinals at St. Louis Rams - December 6th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512060ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Detroit Lions]], he had five tackles and sacked [[Matthew Stafford]] thrice during the 21–14 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Detroit Lions – December 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512130ram.htm |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Meinke |first=Kyle |title=Aaron Donald offers violent reminder of what could have been for Lions |url=http://www.mlive.com/lions/index.ssf/2015/12/aaron_donald_offers_violent_re.html |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=MLive.com |date=December 14, 2015 |language=en-US}}</ref> Donald earned his second NFC Defensive Player of the Week award of the season for his spectacular performance against the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McAtee |first=Joe  |date=December 16, 2015 |title=Rams DT Aaron Donald Named Week 14 NFC DPOW |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2015/12/16/10293346/st-louis-rams-aaron-donald-nfc-defensive-player-of-the-week |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=Turf Show Times|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> During the regular season finale against the 49ers, Donald recorded two solo tackles and a pass deflection in the 19–16 overtime road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=St. Louis Rams at San Francisco 49ers - January 3rd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601030sfo.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Donald finished his second professional season with 69 combined tackles (43 solo), 11 sacks, a pass deflection, and a fumble recovery in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DonaAa00.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He earned a First-team [[All-Pro]] selection for the first time in his NFL career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Broner |first=Tevin |date=January 9, 2016 |title=Three St. Louis Rams Make 2015 All-Pro Team |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2016/1/9/10739378/st-louis-rams-all-pro-aaron-donald-todd-gurley-johnny-hekker |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=Turf Show Times}}</ref> Donald was also a [[Pro Bowl]] selection for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/probowl.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 14th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2016]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2016-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2017: First Defensive Player of the Year Award===
{{See also|2017 Los Angeles Rams season}}
On April 12, 2017, the Rams exercised the fifth-year option on Donald's contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=April 12, 2017 |title=Rams exercise fifth-year option on Aaron Donald |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-exercise-fifth-year-option-on-aaron-donald-0ap3000000799356 |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He did not report to training camp and preseason due to a contract extension dispute. Donald accumulated about $1.4 million in fines due to his non-participation, and each game that he missed cost him one game check from his base salary of $1.8 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gonzalez |first=Alden |date=September 7, 2017 |title=Holdout Aaron Donald expected to miss opener for Rams |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/20619172/holdout-aaron-donald-expected-miss-opener-los-angeles-rams |access-date=September 7, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On September 9, Donald reported to the Rams and passed his physical; however, he did not play in the season-opener against the [[Indianapolis Colts]] the next day, which the Rams won 46–9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=September 9, 2017 |title=Aaron Donald ends holdout, reports to Rams facility |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aaron-donald-ends-holdout-reports-to-rams-facility-0ap3000000841241 |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Donald made his season debut during Week 2 against the Redskins and finished the 27–20 loss with two tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Redskins at Los Angeles Rams - September 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the 49ers on ''Thursday Night Football'', he had three tackles and sacked [[Brian Hoyer]] during the fourth quarter to seal a narrow 41–39 road victory for the Rams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at San Francisco 49ers – September 21st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709210sfo.htm |access-date=September 22, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> From Weeks 6–10, Donald recorded a sack in each of the four games and had a forced fumble in three of them while also deflecting a pass in the Week 10 33–7 victory over the [[Houston Texans]].<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald Game by Game Stats and Performance |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/16716/type/nfl/year/2017 |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=Pro Football Reference}}</ref>

During a Week 12 26–20 victory over the Saints, Donald had five tackles and a sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Los Angeles Rams - November 26th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711260ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the Cardinals, he recorded three solo tackles and sacked [[Blaine Gabbert]] twice during the 32–16 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals - December 3rd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712030crd.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Seahawks, Donald had five tackles, three sacks, and a forced fumble in the 42–7 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Seattle Seahawks – December 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712170sea.htm |access-date=December 18, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 16 against the [[Tennessee Titans]], Donald recorded five tackles and a forced fumble in the 27–23 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Tennessee Titans - December 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240oti.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He did not play in the regular season finale against the 49ers as the Rams opted to rest several starters for the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McAtee |first=Joe |date=December 27, 2017 |title=Rams HC McVay confirms major starters won’t play in Week 17 |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2017/12/27/16824248/los-angeles-rams-week-17-49ers-starters-benched-rest-jared-goff-todd-gurley-whitworth-aaron-donald |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=Turf Show Times|publisher=SB Nation |language=en-US}}</ref>

Donald finished the 2017 season with 41 combined tackles (32 solo), 11 sacks, a career-high five forced fumbles, and a pass deflection in 14 games and starts as the Rams finished the 2017 season atop the [[NFC West]] with an 11–5 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DonaAa00.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Los Angeles Rams Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/ram/2017.htm |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was named to his fourth straight Pro Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2017 |title=NFL announces 2018 Pro Bowl rosters |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/updated-player-rosters-for-2018-pro-bowl-in-orlando-0ap3000000895772 |access-date=December 26, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Donald was also later named a first-team All-Pro for the third time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=January 7, 2018 |title=Aaron Donald wraps up All-Pro season with first NFL playoff appearance |url=https://www.cardiachill.com/2018/1/7/16861190/aaron-donald-2017-all-pro-team-first-nfl-playoff-nfc-wild-card-game-pitt-panthers-los-angeles-rams |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=Cardiac Hill}}</ref> During the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: Atlanta Falcons 26, Los Angeles Rams 13|Wild Card Round]] against the Falcons, he made his postseason debut and finished the 26–13 loss with five tackles and 0.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Atlanta Falcons at Los Angeles Rams - January 6th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801060ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> After a spectacular 2017 season, Donald was named the NFL Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=February 3, 2018 |title=Aaron Donald named NFL Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aaron-donald-named-nfl-defensive-player-of-the-year-0ap3000000913863 |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was ranked seventh by his peers on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2018]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2018-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2018: Second Defensive Player of the Year Award and Super Bowl LIII===
{{See also|2018 Los Angeles Rams season}}

[[File:Aaron Donald.png|thumb|Donald after winning the [[2018 NFC Championship Game|NFC Championship Game]]]]
On August 31, 2018, after holding out all offseason, Donald signed a six-year, $135 million contract extension with $87 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=August 31, 2018 |title=Rams sign Aaron Donald to six-year, $135M extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-sign-aaron-donald-to-6-year-135m-extension-0ap3000000957415 |access-date=October 19, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The deal made him the highest paid defensive player in NFL history until [[Khalil Mack]] signed a $141 million contract with the [[Chicago Bears]] the next day after being traded from the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Khalil Mack agrees to six-year, $141M Bears deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/khalil-mack-agrees-to-six-year-141m-deal-with-bears-0ap3000000957557 |access-date=September 1, 2018 |website=NFL.com |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 4 38–31 victory over the Vikings on ''Thursday Night Football'', Donald had five tackles and his first two sacks of the season on [[Kirk Cousins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Los Angeles Rams - September 27th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809270ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the Seahawks, Donald recorded two tackles and a sack during the narrow 33–31 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Seattle Seahawks - October 7th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201810070sea.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week against the [[Denver Broncos]], he had three tackles and sacked [[Case Keenum]] once in the 23–20 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Denver Broncos - October 14th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201810140den.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 7 against the 49ers, Donald recorded a season-high nine tackles, four sacks on [[C. J. November 4th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811040nor.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 10 36–31 victory over the Seahawks, Donald had four tackles and 2.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Los Angeles Rams - November 11th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201811110ram.htm |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the Chiefs, Donald recorded four tackles and strip-sacked [[Patrick Mahomes]] twice during the [[2018 Kansas City Chiefs–Los Angeles Rams game|54–51 victory]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2018 |title=Rams outlast Chiefs 54-51 in high-octane offensive showcase |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401030972 |access-date=January 17, 2026 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> Following a Week 12 bye, the Rams went on the road to face the Lions. ===2019===

===2022: Injury-shortened season===
{{See also|2022 Los Angeles Rams season}}

On June 7, 2022, the Rams announced they had renegotiated Donald's existing contract extension that he signed in 2018. The deal, which added $40 million over the last three years of the original six-year, $135 million deal, made Donald the first non-quarterback to average over $30 million per season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barshop |first=Sarah |date=June 8, 2022 |title=Sources: DT Aaron Donald gets big raise from Los Angeles Rams in reworked contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34048688/dt-aaron-donald-gets-big-raise-los-angeles-rams-reworked-contract |access-date=June 8, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On August 25, he was part of a joint practice fight between the Rams and Bengals. Donald finished the 2023 season with 53 combined tackles (28 solo), eight sacks, and three pass deflections in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Donald 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DonaAa00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=February 24, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He earned Pro Bowl honors for the 10th time and first-team All-Pro honors for the eighth time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/probowl.htm |access-date=February 24, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL All-Pros |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/allpro.htm |access-date=February 24, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: Detroit Lions 24, Los Angeles Rams 23|Wild Card Round]] against the Lions, Donald had three tackles in the narrow 24–23 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Los Angeles Rams at Detroit Lions - January 14th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401140det.htm |access-date=January 18, 2026 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On March 15, 2024, Donald announced his retirement on social media.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Rams 8-time All-Pro DT Aaron Donald announces retirement after 10 seasons in NFL |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-8-time-all-pro-dt-aaron-donald-announces-retirement-after-10-seasons-in-nfl |access-date=March 15, 2024 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Aaron Donald announces retirement |url=https://www.therams.com/news/aaron-donald-announces-retirement |access-date=March 15, 2024 |website=Los Angeles Rams}}</ref> In a July 2024 interview with former [[Miami Dolphins]] linebacker [[Channing Crowder]], Donald cited feeling more than accomplished in the sport and no longer having the desire or passion to continue the persistent training as reasons for his retirement at age 32.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 6, 2024 |title=Aaron Donald: Opens up, Next Chapter, 1st summer without NFL training camp & family bond |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LBT-axbUXAQ |access-date=February 22, 2026 |website=YouTube |publisher=The Pivot Podcast}}</ref>

Donald's older brother, Archie Jr., was a star linebacker at [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo]] who "bounced around the NFL as an undrafted free agent until retiring in 2012".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archie Donald – Football |url=http://utrockets.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3643 |access-date=August 2, 2019 |website=University of Toledo Athletics |language=en}}</ref> The brothers, who shared bunk beds in their childhood, frequently thought about one day helping their parents retire, which became one of the driving forces in Aaron's career.<ref name=Gonzalez/> On April 27, 2020, Donald revealed on Twitter that he had graduated from the University of Pittsburgh with a degree in communications.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Megan  |date=April 27, 2020 |title=Rams' Aaron Donald Earns Degree, Graduates from Pittsburgh |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2889020-rams-aaron-donald-earns-degree-graduates-from-pittsburgh |access-date=July 5, 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, Donald and his wife Erica had a son named Aaric. '''Aaron Colvin''' (born October 2, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]] and was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the fourth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Houston Texans]] and [[Washington Redskins]].

==Early life==
Colvin attended [[Owasso High School]] in [[Owasso, Oklahoma]], where he played [[high school football]]. He recorded 72 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], two [[interceptions]] while breaking up 10 passes and scoring five [[touchdowns]] in 2009. He was recognized as first-team All-State by both the ''[[Tulsa World]]'' and ''[[The Oklahoman]]'' in 2009, and was also the district 6A-4 defensive player of the year.

Considered a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', he was rated as the 31st best [[cornerback]] prospect in the nation.<ref>[http://rivals.yahoo.com/oklahoma/football/recruiting/player-Aaron-Colvin-87646 Aaron Colvin - Yahoo Sports]</ref> He committed to [[University of Oklahoma|Oklahoma]] over offers from [[Oklahoma State University|Oklahoma State]], [[University of Missouri|Missouri]] and [[University of Tulsa|Tulsa]].<ref>[http://www.crimsonandcreammachine.com/2009/7/26/963964/aaron-colvin-commits-to-sooners Aaron Colvin Commits To Oklahoma]</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Colvin played in all 14 games, primarily on [[special teams]] and as a backup cornerback. He amassed 21 tackles, three for loss, three [[pass breakups]] and one forced [[fumble]]. In 2011, he was moved to [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|strong safety]] and led the team with 84 tackles, including 4.5 for loss, and six pass breakups.<ref>[http://newsok.com/ous-aaron-colvin-moved-to-safety-coaches-impressed/article/3551262 OU Coaches Impressed By Colvin's Move To Safety]</ref> As a junior in 2012, Colvin was moved back to cornerback.<ref name="b219">{{cite web | last=Chatmon | first=Brandon | title=OU's Aaron Colvin comfortable at 'true position' | website=ESPN.com | date=2012-08-14 | url=https://www.espn.com/colleges/oklahoma/football/story/_/id/8269717/aaron-colvin-oklahoma-sooners-moves-back-cornerback | access-date=2024-12-01}}</ref> He started all 13 games, and finished tied for second in the [[Big 12 Conference]] with four interceptions. He also recorded 61 tackles, including 2.5 for loss, and eleven pass breakups while earning first-team All-Big 12 honors. In 2013, he played in 11 games, recording 55 tackles, including five for loss, one interception and three pass breakups. He ended his career earning a first-team All-Big 12 selection. Overall, Colvin finished his Oklahoma career playing in 50 games with 36 starts, recording 234 tackles, 3.5 sacks, 5 interceptions, 23 pass deflections, 3 fumble recoveries and 1 forced fumble.<ref> https://soonersports.com/sports/football/roster/aaron-colvin/2886</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
====2014====
The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] selected Colvin in the fourth round (114th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. Colvin was the 12th cornerback drafted in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The pick that was used to select Colvin was acquired in a trade that sent [[Eugene Monroe]] to the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>[http://newsok.com/oklahoma-football-jacksonville-jaguars-draft-cornerback-aaron-colvin-in-the-fourth-round/article/4748434 Jacksonville Jaguars draft cornerback Aaron Colvin in the fourth round]</ref> On May 21, 2014, the Jaguars signed Colvin to a four-year, $2.67 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $453,152.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Aaron Colvin contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/houston-texans/aaron-colvin-14525/ |access-date=October 23, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

His knee injury sidelined him for the Jaguars’ entire [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], preseason, and their first ten regular seasons games. On November 12, 2014, the Jaguars officially activated Colvin off of their [[physically unable to perform]] list.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars activate OU's Aaron Colvin |url=https://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/ousportsextra/jacksonville-jaguars-activate-ou-s-aaron-colvin/article_0a2b09a5-a94b-59c9-bf93-cc67a2263c96.html |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=TulsaWorld.com |author=Long, Mark |date=November 12, 2014}}</ref> Upon joining the active roster, Colvin was named the third cornerback on the [[depth chart]] by head coach [[Gus Bradley]]. He began the season behind starting cornerbacks [[Dwayne Gratz]] and [[Demetrius McCray]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars Depth Chart: 12/01/2014 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/166/JAX |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On November 23, 2014, Colvin made his professional regular season debut and recorded one tackle during the Jaguars’ 23–3 loss at the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 12. On November 30, 2014, Colvin recorded four combined tackles, broke up a pass, and returned a fumble for a 41-yard touchdown during a 25–24 win against the [[New York Giants]]. Colvin recovered a fumble after the ball was fumbled by Giants’ tight end [[Larry Donnell]] after it was jarred loose by Gratz during the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=New York Giants at Jacksonville Jaguars - November 30th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411300jax.htm |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The Jaguars went on to complete a 21-point comeback, the largest in team history, and earn their second win of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=National Football League Game Summary|url=http://www.nfl.com/liveupdate/gamecenter/56353/JAC_Gamebook.pdf|website=NFL.com|access-date=May 6, 2015}}</ref> In Week 16, he collected a season-high seven solo tackles and deflected a pass during a 23–13 victory against the [[Tennessee Titans]]. On December 28, 2014, Colvin earned his first career start and recorded four combined tackles during a 23–17 loss at the [[Houston Texans]] in Week 17.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stays: Aaron Colvin (2014) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/aaroncolvin/2543501/gamelogs?season=2014 |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season in 2014 with 27 combined tackles (23 solo), two pass deflections, one fumble recovery, and one touchdown in six games and one start.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Aaron Colvin (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/aaroncolvin/2543501/careerstats |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2015====
Throughout training camp, Colvin competed to be a starting cornerback against Gratz and McCray.<ref>{{cite web |title=Demetrius McCray competing to hold onto his starting job |url=https://www.firstcoastnews.com/mobile/article/sports/demetrius-mccray-competing-to-hold-onto-his-starting-job/123396645 |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=firstcoastnews.com |date=June 2, 2015}}</ref> Bradley named Colvin and [[Davon House]] the starting cornerbacks to start the regular season in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars Depth Chart: 09/01/2015 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/175/JAX |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On October 4, 2015, Colvin recorded six combined tackles and made his first career sack on Colts’ quarterback [[Andrew Luck]] during a 16–13 loss at the Colts in Week 4. In Week 16, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles as the Jaguars lost 38–17 at the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stays: Aaron Colvin (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/aaroncolvin/2543501/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Colvin finished the [[2017 NFL season]] with a career-high 73 combined tackles (60 solo), seven pass deflections, four sacks, and one forced fumble in 16 games and 15 starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2016====
On April 8, 2016, it was announced that Colvin had violated the NFL’s performance-enhancing substances policy and would be suspended for the first four games of the [[2016 NFL season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Down to 53: LB Davis, OG Bernadeau released|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Down-to-53-LB-Davis-OG-Bernadeau-released/d39aa0b3-fc8a-47df-9a6d-c71d01ffa980|last=Oehser|first=John|website=Jaguars.com|access-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510151911/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-jaguarsnews/down-to-53-lb-davis-og-bernadeau-released/d39aa0b3-fc8a-47df-9a6d-c71d01ffa980|archive-date=May 10, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Colvin entered training camp as a backup cornerback after the Jaguars signed free agent cornerback [[Prince Amukamara]] and drafted cornerback [[Jalen Ramsey]] in the first round (fifth overall) during the [[2016 NFL draft]]. Upon his return from suspension, Colvin was named the fourth cornerback on the Jaguars’ depth chart. He began Week 6 listed behind Davon House, Jalen Ramsey, and Prince Amukamara.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars Depth Chart: 10/01/2016 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/189/JAX |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 9, Colvin collected a season-high seven combined tackles during a 19–14 loss at the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. On December 18, 2016, the Jaguars fired Bradley after they fell to a 2–12 record. Assistant head coach [[Doug Marrone]] was named the interim head coach for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaguars fire Gus Bradley after four seasons of historically bad football |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/jaguars-fire-gus-bradley-after-four-seasons-of-historically-bad-football/ |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=CBSSports.com |author=Wilson, Ryan |date=December 18, 2016}}</ref> On December 23, 2016, the Jaguars placed Colvin on [[injured reserve]] due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aaron Colvin, Chris Reed placed on injured reserve|url=http://www.bigcatcountry.com/2016/12/23/14070810/aaron-colvin-chris-reed-placed-on-injured-reserve|author=Day, Ryan|website=BigCatCountry.com|date=December 23, 2016}}</ref> Colvin finished the 2016 season with 22 combined tackles (18 solo) and one pass deflection in ten games and four starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2017====
Colvin entered training camp slated as the third cornerback on the depth chart. Head coach Doug Marrone retained [[Todd Wash]] as the defensive coordinator and named Colvin the third cornerback on the depth chart to start the season, behind Jalen Ramsey and [[A. J. Bouye]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Jacksonville Jaguars Depth Chart: 09/01/2017 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/JAX |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 5, Colvin collected a season-high ten combined tackles (nine solo) during a 30–9 win at the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He played in all 16 games with five starts, recording 45 combined tackles (28 solo) and five passes defensed.<ref name="career"/> Colvin was one of two cornerbacks not to allow any touchdowns during the season. He played 672 defensive snaps and received an overall grade of 80.0 from [[Pro Football Focus]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Aaron Colvin didn't allow a single touchdown in 2017 after 672 snaps, per PFF |url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2018/02/21/aaron-colvin-didnt-allow-a-single-touchdown-in-2017-after-672-snaps-per-pff/ |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=jaguarswire.usatoday.com |author=Johnson, Jay |date=February 21, 2018}}</ref>

The Jaguars finished first in the [[AFC South]] with a 10–6 record and earned a playoff berth. On January 7, 2018, Colvin appeared in his first career playoff game and recorded one solo tackle, deflected a pass, and made his first career interception as the Jaguars defeated the [[Buffalo Bills]] 10–3 in the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] Wildcard Game. Colvin intercepted a pass by Bills’ quarterback [[Tyrod Taylor]], that was originally intended for tight end [[Logan Thomas]] and was deflected by Jaguars’ linebacker [[Myles Jack]] during the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Wild Card - Buffalo Bills at Jacksonville Jaguars - January 7th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801070jax.htm |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The following week, the Jaguars defeated the Steelers 45–42 in the AFC Divisional Round before being eliminated from the playoffs after a 24–20 loss at the [[New England Patriots]] in the [[AFC Championship Game]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player Stats: Aaron Colvin (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/aaroncolvin/2543501/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On March 13, 2018, the Texans signed Colvin to a four-year, $34 million contract that includes $18 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $4 million.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Aaron Colvin set to sign with Texans|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/13/aaron-colvin-set-to-sign-with-texans/|author=Smith, Michael David|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=March 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-Colvin-Fulton-Henderson-Kelemete/c29985ce-24e1-4081-a318-f04dd0bb110e|title=Texans sign Colvin, Fulton, Henderson, Kelemete|work=HoustonTexans.com|date=March 15, 2018}}</ref> He entered training camp slated as the first-team nickelback and third cornerback on the depth chart. Head coach [[Bill O'Brien (American football)|Bill O’Brien]] named Colvin the third cornerback on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind [[Johnathan Joseph]] and [[Kevin Johnson (cornerback)|Kevin Johnson]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Unofficial Depth Chart: Texans at Patriots |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/unofficial-depth-chart-texans-at-patriots |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=September 4, 2018}}</ref> On September 11, 2018, Colvin became a starting cornerback after Kevin Johnson was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web |title=Texans corner Kevin Johnson placed on injured reserve |url=https://m.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-Kevin-Johnson-placed-injured-reserve-13221752.php |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=Chron.com |date=September 11, 2018}}</ref> He was inactive for three games (Weeks 5-7) due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Texans unsure if Aaron Colvin will be able to play again this season|url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/24861837/aaron-colvin-houston-texans-indefinitely-ankle-injury |access-date=October 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Bar shop, Sarah |date=October 1, 2018}}</ref>

On September 10, 2019, Colvin was released by the Texans after giving up a catch on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' lto [[Ted Ginn Jr.]] to put the Saints in [[field goal]] range that possibly helped cost the Texans the game with [[Wil Lutz]] nailing a 58-yard field goal and Colvin's team losing 30–28.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans release Aaron Colvin, sign Phillip Gaines|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/09/10/texans-release-aaron-colvin-sign-phillip-gaines/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=September 10, 2019}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins / Football Team===
[[File:Aaron Colvin 2019.jpg|thumb|Colvin with the Washington Redskins in 2019]]
On September 13, 2019, Colvin signed a one-year contract with the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Redskins sign ex-Texans cornerback Aaron Colvin|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/redskins-sign-ex-texans-cornerback-aaron-colvin-0ap3000001054290|access-date=September 13, 2019 |website=[[NFL.com]] |author=Jeremy Bergman|date=September 13, 2019}}</ref> Colvin re-signed on May 14, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Bill-in-Bangkok |title=Redskins re-sign cornerback Aaron Colvin |url=https://www.hogshaven.com/2020/5/14/21258754/redskins-re-sign-cornerback-aaron-colvin |website=Hogs Haven}}</ref> He was released during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020, and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jhabvala |first1=Nicki |last2=Fortier |first2=Sam |title=Alex Smith avoids Washington Football Team's cuts, will remain on 53-man roster |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/09/05/washington-roster-cuts/ |website=Washington Post}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Washington Football Team Signs 13 Players To Its Practice Squad|url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/washington-football-team-signs-12-players-practice-squad|website=WashingtonFootball.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref> His practice squad contract with the team expired after the season on January 18, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Three players set free |url=https://www.fantasyguru.com/football-team-three-players-set-free/ |website=FantasyGuru.com |date=January 18, 2021 |access-date=February 18, 2021 |archive-date=February 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228115818/https://www.fantasyguru.com/football-team-three-players-set-free/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the fifth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[South Florida Bulls football|South Florida]] and [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]]. ==Early life== Lynch attended [[Island Coast High School]] in [[Cape Coral, Florida]].{{Cite web |title=Aaron Lynch's High School Timeline |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/aaron-lynch/InMD0PTmEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm |access-date=September 10, 2019 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}} He led the team to 11–2 record and Florida 2B state semifinal playoff appearance as senior in 2010. He also recorded 31 solo [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and 10.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] during senior campaign. He played in the [[U.S Army All-American Bowl]] in [[San Antonio, Texas]] in 2011. Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Lynch was listed as the No. 3 [[defensive end]] in the nation.[https://sports.yahoo.com/notredame/football/recruiting/player-Aaron-Lynch-107934 Aaron Lynch – Yahoo Sports] After de-committing from [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]], he re-committed to Notre Dame over offers from [[Florida Gators football|Florida]] and [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]].[http://www.irishsportsdaily.com/recruiting/notre-dame-football-recruiting/3980-aaron-lynch-commits-to-notre-dame Aaron Lynch Commits To Notre Dame] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201175134/http://www.irishsportsdaily.com/recruiting/notre-dame-football-recruiting/3980-aaron-lynch-commits-to-notre-dame |date=February 1, 2014 }} ==College career== In 2011, Lynch enrolled a semester early at Notre Dame and was able to participate in spring practice. He worked his way onto the second-team and dominated in the annual Blue-Gold game.{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2011 |title=Five things we learned: The 82nd Blue-Gold game |url=http://irish.nbcsports.com/2011/04/16/five-things-we-learned-the-82nd-blue-gold-game/ |access-date=September 10, 2019 |website=Inside the Irish |language=en-US}} In his freshman season, he played in 12 games, starting in 6 of them. He recorded 33 tackles including 7 [[tackles for loss]], a team high 5.5 sacks, and a team high of 14 quarterback hurries. He was awarded a 1st team selection on The 11th annual [[Football Writers Association of America]] Freshman [[All-America]] Team.[http://www.sportswriters.net/fwaa/news/2011/allamerica120109.html FWAA NAMES 2011 FRESHMAN ALL-AMERICA TEAM] In April 2012, Lynch decided to transfer from Notre Dame, citing a desire to return closer to his home.{{cite web | last=Fortuna | first=Matt | title=Notre Dame freshman DE Lynch to transfer | website=ESPN.com | date=2012-04-13 | url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/ncf/story/_/id/7809682/defensive-end-aaron-lynch-transferring-notre-dame | access-date=2024-09-09}} After pondering his options, he announced his transfer to [[South Florida Bulls football|USF]].{{cite web | last=Fortuna | first=Matt | title=South Florida adding ex-Notre Dame DE Lynch | website=ESPN.com | date=2012-04-23 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/7847127/south-florida-bulls-adding-former-notre-dame-fighting-irish-de-aaron-lynch | access-date=2024-09-09}} He applied for a waiver to play immediately but the [[NCAA]] denied his request, forcing him to sit out the 2012 season.{{Cite web |last=Auman |first=Greg |date=August 23, 2012 |title=NCAA denies hardship waiver for USF Bulls transfer Aaron Lynch |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/college/ncaa-denies-hardship-waiver-for-usf-bulls-transfer-aaron-lynch/1247338/ |access-date=September 10, 2019 |website=Tampa Bay Times |language=en}} As a junior, Lynch led the Bulls with six sacks and 12.5 tackles for loss, playing in all 12 games. He finished with 30 total tackles and added a [[fumble]] recovery returned for a [[touchdown]] in a 13–10 win over the [[2013 UConn Huskies football team|Connecticut Huskies]].{{Cite web |last=Eaton-Robb |first=Pat |date=October 12, 2013|agency=Associated Press |title=USF slips past UConn, 13–10 |url=https://www.news-journalonline.com/news/20131012/usf-slips-past-uconn-13-10 |access-date=September 11, 2019 |website=Daytona Beach News-Journal}} Lynch had a strong finish to the season despite the Bulls' 3–9 record, totaling all six sacks in the last seven games.{{Cite web |title=2013 South Florida Bulls Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/south-florida/2013-schedule.html |access-date=September 11, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] 2014 NFL draft.{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Taylor |date=May 10, 2014 |title=San Francisco 49ers Draft USF LB Aaron Lynch |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/san-francisco-49ers-draft-usf-lb-aaron-lynch-12994879 |access-date=July 3, 2017 |website=49ers.com}} Lynch was given an opportunity and assisted on four tackles and made two solo tackles on November 9 against the [[New Orleans Saints]]. His six tackles in addition to his [[pass defended]] helped the 49ers excel in an overtime battle to defeat the Saints and remain in the playoff picture. '''Aaron Dantianto Pearson''' (born August 22, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played three seasons with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the Chiefs in the eleventh round of the [[1986 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Itawamba Junior College]] and [[Mississippi State University]].

==Early life and college==
Aaron Dantianto Pearson was born August 22, 1964, in [[Gadsden, Alabama]].<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/p/pear01000.html | title=Aaron Pearson | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref> He attended Gadsden High School.<ref name="pfa"/>

Pearson first played [[college football]] at [[Itawamba Junior College]] from 1982 to 1983.<ref name="pfa"/> He then transferred to [[Mississippi State University]], where he was a two-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State Bulldogs]] from 1984 to 1985.<ref name="pfa"/> He was named second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] by the [[Associated Press]] in 1984.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1320&dat=19841204&id=urMRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=qekDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6702,1282112|work=Gainesville Sun|date=December 4, 1984|title=All-SEC team}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Pearson was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the 11th round, with the 285th overall pick, of the [[1986 NFL draft]].<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PearAa20.htm | title=Aaron Pearson | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref> He officially signed with the team on July 23.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 15 games for the Chiefs during his rookie year in 1986.<ref name="pfr"/> He also appeared in one playoff game.<ref name="pfr"/> Pearson appeared in 12 games, starting nine, during the strike-shortened 1987 season.<ref name="pfr"/> He played in all 16 games, starting ten, in 1988.<ref name="pfr"/> He became a free agent after the 1988 season and re-signed with the Chiefs.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on July 23, 1989.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/p/pear01000.html | title=Aaron Pearson Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archive | accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In May 1992, Pearson was shot in a dispute after breaking a car's windshield with his fists.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ex-chief is shot in dispute |url=https://tulsaworld.com/archive/ex-chief-is-shot-in-dispute/article_faae9f64-f4e2-5dea-857d-9c955a0e6fa2.html |website=Tulsa World |date=28 May 1992 |access-date=23 February 2021}}</ref>

'''Aaron Randal Ripkowski''' (born December 20, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]], and was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the sixth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Ripkowski attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Dayton High School (Texas)|Dayton High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Dayton's Ripkowski picked by Packers in NFL draft |url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/dayton/sports/article/Dayton-s-Ripkowski-picked-by-Packers-in-NFL-9672937.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093403/https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/dayton/sports/article/Dayton-s-Ripkowski-picked-by-Packers-in-NFL-9672937.php |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref>

==College career==
Ripkowski attended the [[University of Oklahoma]], where he played on the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Sooners]] from 2011 to 2014 under head coach [[Bob Stoops]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oklahoma Sooners: Aaron Ripkowski |url=http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?atclid=208409605 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028083519/http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?atclid=208409605 |archive-date=October 28, 2016 |access-date=October 27, 2016 |website=SoonerSports.com}}</ref> In the 2013 season, he had one [[Reception (gridiron football)|reception]] for a three-yard [[touchdown]] on the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ripkowski 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-ripkowski-1/gamelog/2013/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428011919/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-ripkowski-1/gamelog/2013/ |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2014 season, he had seven receptions for 38 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown to go along with six [[Carry (gridiron football)|carries]] for 13 [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushing]] yards and three rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ripkowski 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-ripkowski-1/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428011914/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-ripkowski-1/gamelog/2014/ |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In four years at Oklahoma, he appeared in 47 games and started 17.
