===Green Bay Packers===
====2015 season====
Ripkowski was selected in the sixth round (206th overall) by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022150939/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |archive-date=October 22, 2018 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 8, 2015, he signed a contract with the Packers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 8, 2015 |title=Packers sign five draft choices |url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-press-release/article-1/packers-sign-five-draft-choices/cdf08670-7daf-482d-b003-e5d2e262ac00 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170927112202/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-press-release/article-1/packers-sign-five-draft-choices/cdf08670-7daf-482d-b003-e5d2e262ac00 |archive-date=September 27, 2017 |access-date=August 17, 2016 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> In his rookie season, Ripkowski was the Packers' backup [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] behind veteran [[John Kuhn]]. He appeared in 15 games, finishing the year with nine [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] on [[special teams]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers: Aaron Ripkowski |url=http://www.packers.com/team/roster/aaron-ripkowski/2fb6e242-2da7-4d48-8688-0a1de0df6578 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180416173728/http://www.packers.com/team/roster/aaron-ripkowski/2fb6e242-2da7-4d48-8688-0a1de0df6578 |archive-date=April 16, 2018 |access-date=August 17, 2016 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> Ripkowski recorded his first career NFL reception, an 18-yard catch and run from quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]] against the [[Carolina Panthers]] in Week 9.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Carolina Panthers – November 8th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511080car.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101211145/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511080car.htm |archive-date=January 1, 2018 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, he appeared in fifteen regular season games and two playoff games. He mostly contributed on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ripkowski 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RipkAa00/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093646/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RipkAa00/gamelog/2015/ |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2016 season====
In 2016, entering his second year, Ripkowski became the starting fullback after the Packers did not re-sign John Kuhn.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spofford |first=Mike |date=July 12, 2016 |title=Countdown to Camp: Spotlight remains on Eddie Lacy |url=https://www.packers.com/news/countdown-to-camp-spotlight-remains-on-eddie-lacy-17322886 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181125115400/https://www.packers.com/news/countdown-to-camp-spotlight-remains-on-eddie-lacy-17322886 |archive-date=November 25, 2018 |access-date=August 17, 2016 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> As the 2016 season progressed, Ripkowski's role expanded due to injuries to running backs [[Eddie Lacy]] and [[James Starks]]. He finished the 2016 regular season with 34 carries for 150 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to go along with nine receptions for 46 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown. He also contributed on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ripkowski 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RipkAa00/gamelog/2016 |url-status=live ====2017 season====
In the 2017 season, Ripkowski appeared in all 16 games and recorded five carries for 13 rushing yards and seven receptions for 39 receiving yards. He contributed on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Ripkowski 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RipkAa00/gamelog/2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093820/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RipkAa00/gamelog/2017 |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On September 1, 2018, Ripkowski was released by the Packers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Packers announce roster moves |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405075805/https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-1 |archive-date=April 5, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=Packers.com}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On January 31, 2019, Ripkowski signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=January 31, 2019 |title=Chiefs Sign FB Aaron Ripkowski To Futures Deal |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/chiefs-sign-fb-aaron-ripkowski-to-futures-deal/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407011432/https://nfltraderumors.co/chiefs-sign-fb-aaron-ripkowski-to-futures-deal/ |archive-date=April 7, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=NFL Trade Rumors}}</ref> He was waived by the Chiefs on May 3.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=May 3, 2019 |title=Chiefs cut three, including Aaron Ripkowski |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/05/03/chiefs-cut-three-including-aaron-ripkowski/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406094308/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/05/03/chiefs-cut-three-including-aaron-ripkowski/ |archive-date=April 6, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Aaron Green''' (born October 15, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]] and was signed by the [[Los Angeles Rams]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2016.

==Early life==
Green attended [[James Madison High School (San Antonio)|James Madison High School]]. He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]]. He transferred to [[Texas Christian University]] after his freshman season. He sat out the 2012 season to comply with the [[NCAA]] transfer rules.

He became a starter for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|Horned Frogs]] as a junior, leading the team with 922 rushing yards and 9 touchdowns on a 7.1 per carry average. As senior, he appeared in 13 games (10 starts), finishing seventh in school history with 1,272 rushing yards on the season.

'''Aaron LaRae Jones Sr.''' (born December 2, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP Miners]] and was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the fifth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. In seven seasons with the Packers, Jones led the league in rushing touchdowns in 2019, made the [[Pro Bowl]] in 2020, and ranks third in the team's all-time rushing yards list.

==Early life==
Jones was born in [[Savannah, Georgia]], to Vurgess and Alvin Jones Sr., two career [[non-commissioned officer#United States|non-commissioned officers]] in the [[United States Army|US Army]]. He and his twin brother [[Alvin Jones (American football)|Alvin Jr.]], older brother Xavier, and sister Chelsirae moved around often due to their parents' postings, living in [[Germany]], [[Kentucky]], [[Tennessee]], [[Virginia]], and near the [[Mexican border (U.S.)|Mexican border]] in the city of El Paso.<ref name="Kaplan1">{{Cite web |last=Kaplan |first=Emily |author-link=Emily Kaplan |date=January 9, 2020 |title=Aaron Jones is finally free – and ready for the playoffs |url=https://www.espn.ph/nfl/story/_/id/28446151/packers-back-aaron-jones-free-ready-run-opportunity |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

As a child, Jones looked up to [[Emmitt Smith]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Serby |first=Steve |date=January 11, 2020 |title=Packers' Aaron Jones on beating odds despite being overlooked |url=https://nypost.com/2020/01/10/packers-aaron-jones-on-beating-odds-despite-being-overlooked/ |access-date=October 10, 2022 |website=New York Post |language=en-US}}</ref> He attended and played [[high school football]] for [[Burges High School (El Paso, Texas)|Burges High School]] in [[El Paso, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=De Leon |first=Gloria |date=October 9, 2017 |title=Burges coach, players proud of Aaron Jones' success in the NFL |url=http://kfoxtv.com/news/local/burges-coach-players-proud-of-aaron-jones-success-in-the-nfl |access-date=March 4, 2018 |website=KFOX}}</ref> He had a three-star composite rating from [[247Sports.com]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones, Burges, Athlete |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Aaron-Jones-23052/high-school-36710/ |access-date=February 1, 2019 |website=247Sports}}</ref> His father retired before his senior year and started a marketing company to jump-start the recruiting process for his sons.<ref name=Kaplan1/>

==College career==
Jones attended and played [[college football]] for the [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP Miners]] from 2013 to 2016 under head coach [[Sean Kugler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-jones-6.html |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a freshman, Jones played in nine football games. In his collegiate debut, against [[2013 New Mexico Lobos football team|New Mexico]], he had 11 carries for 127 yards and two rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Mexico at Texas-El Paso Box Score, September 7, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-07-texas-el-paso.html |access-date=March 4, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> On October 26, against [[2013 Rice Owls football team|Rice]], he had a season-high 186 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UTEP at Rice Box Score, October 26, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-26-rice.html |access-date=March 4, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2013 season with 811 rushing yards, four rushing touchdowns, and four receptions for 14 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aaron-jones-6/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=March 4, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

As a sophomore, Jones played in 12 games. He started the 2014 season off with three strong performances. This made Jones the most prolific rusher in UTEP Miners history and a top player. In terms of rushing yards, he had five of the school's top 12 games, and school records of 17 games with 100+ yards rushing, and five with 200+ yards. He holds the record for most rushing yards in a career (4,114), season (1,773; also fifth his second year), and career yards per game (117.5) including the 2nd- and 6th-best seasons in school history (147.8 in 2016; 110.1 in 2014). He is second all-time with 33 rushing touchdowns, including the school's 3rd- and 7th-best seasons (17 in 2016; 11 in 2014). His 4,760 career all-purpose yards and 136.0 per game average are both second all-time and included the school's fourth- and eighth-best seasons. He has three of the school's 10 longest rushing plays, including the record 91-yarder from his short junior season. His 240 career points scored is 4th all-time, and 2nd among non-kickers.<ref name="MG" />

After injuries to [[Ty Montgomery]] and [[Jamaal Williams]], Jones came into the ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'' game against the [[Chicago Bears]] in Week 4. In the game, he had 13 carries for 49 yards and his first career rushing touchdown in the 35–14 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers – September 28th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709280gnb.htm |access-date=November 5, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 5 against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Jones tallied 19 carries for 125 yards. He also had one lone target, for a nine-yard gain. In the second quarter, Jones rushed up the middle for a seven-yard touchdown, which was the second touchdown of his career. In Week 7, against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he had 17 carries for 131 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Green Bay Packers – October 22nd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710220gnb.htm |access-date=November 5, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Overall, he finished his rookie season with 448 rushing yards (second on the team to fellow rookie Jamaal Williams, ninth among NFL rookies), a team-leading four rushing touchdowns, nine receptions, and 22 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneAa00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=March 4, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

|website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 17, in a 41–17 win over the Vikings, he had 14 carries for 111 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers – January 1st, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202301010gnb.htm |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Jones rushed for a personal best 1,121 yards on 213 carries. He had two rushing touchdowns and five receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneAa00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=July 23, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 64th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2023]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2023-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2023 season====
In Week 1 against the Bears, Jones had one rushing and one receiving touchdown and 127 scrimmage yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Chicago Bears – September 10th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309100chi.htm |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Jones suffered a hamstring injury in that game and did not return.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reischel |first=Rob |date=September 17, 2023 |title=Report: The Green Bay Packers Won't Have Aaron Jones Or Christian Watson Today |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/robreischel/2023/09/17/report-the-green-bay-packers-wont-have-aaron-jones-or-christian-watson-today/ |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> He was inactive the next week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kownack |first=Bobby |date=September 17, 2023 |title=Aaron Jones, Christian Watson inactive for Packers-Falcons |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/aaron-jones-christian-watson-inactive-for-packers-falcons |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Jones missed six games in the season, but still finished with 656 rushing yards, 233 receiving yards and three touchdowns. In back-to-back-to-back must-win games for the Packers to earn a playoff berth in the team's first season with [[Jordan Love]] as the starting quarterback, Jones recorded at least 130 offensive yards in each game, helping secure a wild-card playoff spot.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aaron Jones 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneAa00/gamelog/2023/ |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=January 16, 2024}}</ref>

Jones ran for 118 yards with three touchdowns on 21 attempts in a [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: Green Bay Packers 48, Dallas Cowboys 32|Wild Card Round]] 48–32 win over the Cowboys at [[AT&T Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |agency=[[Associated Press]] |title=Jordan Love and the Packers pull a wild-card stunner, beating Dak Prescott and the Cowboys 48–32 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/gametracker/recap/NFL_20240114_GB@DAL/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=January 16, 2024|date=January 15, 2024}}</ref> In that performance, Jones set the franchise record for playoff rushing touchdowns with seven and tied the record for most rushing touchdowns by a Packer in a playoff game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most rushing touchdowns in a single game, postseason, Green Bay Packers |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/most-playoff-rushing-tds-by-a-packer-in-a-game |access-date=January 17, 2024 |website=Statmuse}}</ref>

In a season-ending 24–21 [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 49ers 24, Green Bay Packers 21|Divisional Round]] loss to the 49ers, Jones became the first player in the more than 100-year history of the Green Bay Packers to record five consecutive 100-yard rushing games.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wilde |first1=Jason |title=5 things we learned from the Packers' 24–21 loss to the 49ers in the divisional playoffs |url=https://madison.com/sports/professional/nfl/packers-49ers-5-things-learned-love/article_66ba4ed2-b3ce-11ee-a044-d71b4ba14b33.html#tracking-source=ml-homepage&recomm_id=45fc3274cb443706e04a324185a437dd |access-date=January 22, 2024 |publisher=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |date=January 21, 2024}}</ref>

On March 11, 2024, Jones was released by the Packers after seven seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 11, 2024 |title=Packers release RB Aaron Jones |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-release-rb-aaron-jones |access-date=May 3, 2024 |website=Packers.com}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On March 12, 2024, Jones signed a one-year contract with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Lindsey |date=March 12, 2024 |title=Vikings Agree to Terms with Former Packers RB Aaron Jones |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/aaron-jones-running-back-agree-to-terms-packers |access-date=March 12, 2024 |website=Minnesota Vikings}}</ref> In Week 12, against the [[2024 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], he had 22 carries for 106 yards and a touchdown in the 30–27 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears - November 24th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202411240chi.htm |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 2024 season, Jones had 255 carries for 1,138 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns to go with 51 receptions for 408 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneAa00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Jones was ranked 98th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2025]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Peters | first=Craig | title=Aaron Jones, Sr., Lands at No. 98 on NFL’s Top 100 of 2025 | website=Vikings.com | date=2025-07-01 | url=https://www.vikings.com/news/aaron-jones-nfl-top-100-players-2025#:~:text=Aaron%20Jones%2C%20Sr.%2C%20Lands,NFL's%20Top%20100%20of%202025&text=The%20positive%20impacts%20made%20by,room%20%E2%80%94%20and%20across%20the%20NFL. | access-date=2025-08-20}}</ref>

On March 9, 2025, Jones re-signed with the Vikings on a two-year, $20 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=March 9, 2025 |title=Sources: Vikings re-signing RB Aaron Jones to 2-year, $20M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/44182013/sources-vikings-re-signing-rb-aaron-jones-2-year-20m-deal |access-date=March 12, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> After starting Minnesota's first two games of the year, he was placed on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury on September 16.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 16, 2025 |title=Source: Vikings place Aaron Jones on injured reserve |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46284999/sources-vikings-place-aaron-jones-injured-reserve |access-date=October 12, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Jones was activated on October 22, ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup against the [[2025 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Seifert | first=Kevin | title=Vikings activate RB Aaron Jones ahead of Chargers game | website=ESPN.com | date=2025-10-23 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46700714/vikings-activate-rb-aaron-jones-ahead-charges-game | access-date=2026-02-05}}</ref> In the 2025 season, he appeared in 12 games and finished with 132 carries for 548 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to go with 28 receptions for 199 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Jones 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneAa00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
During his tenure in Green Bay, Jones was known for wearing [[wraparound sunglasses|wraparound]] [[Oakley, Inc.|Oakley sunglasses]] and a [[sombrero]] decorated in Packers colors when arriving at a stadium before a game, on the sidelines, and in postgame interviews.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bleier |first=Evan |date=November 27, 2020 |title=Green Bay RB Aaron Jones Explains His Signature Shades and Sombrero |url=https://www.insidehook.com/article/sports/packers-aaron-jones-sideline-shades-signature-sombrero |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211031221604/https://www.insidehook.com/article/sports/packers-aaron-jones-sideline-shades-signature-sombrero |archive-date=October 31, 2021 |access-date=October 29, 2021 |website=The Inside Hook }}</ref> The sombrero is an homage to his hometown of El Paso, a [[List of U.S. cities with large Hispanic populations|majority-Hispanic]] city.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rogers |first1=Joshua |title=Why does Aaron Jones wear a sombrero, and what are his sunglasses? |url=https://www.thefocus.news/sports/nfl/why-does-aaron-jones-wear-a-sombrero-and-what-are-his-sunglasses/ |website=The Focus |access-date=December 20, 2022 |date=December 5, 2022}}</ref> He also pays tribute to El Paso in his signature touchdown celebration, in which he holds up nine, one, and five fingers in quick succession before flexing his bicep (El Paso is covered by [[area code 915]]).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rogers |first1=Joshua |title=Who was Aaron Jones' father, as Packers star loses necklace during Lions game? |url=https://www.thefocus.news/sports/nfl/who-was-aaron-jones-father/ |website=The Focus |access-date=December 20, 2022 |date=September 21, 2021 |archive-date=December 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221055325/https://www.thefocus.news/sports/nfl/who-was-aaron-jones-father/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Jones graduated from UTEP on May 12, 2018, with a degree in [[Interdisciplinarity|multidisciplinary studies]], fulfilling a promise he had previously made to his parents that he would finish school even if drafted into the NFL.<ref name=Kaplan1/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez |first=Alexandria |date=May 12, 2018 |title=NFL player Aaron Jones graduates from UTEP |url=https://kfoxtv.com/news/local/nfl-player-aaron-jones-graduates-from-utep-05-13-2018#:~:text=EL%20PASO%2C%20Texas%20%E2%80%94%20After%20getting,graduated%20from%20UTEP%20Saturday%20morning. |access-date=September 19, 2022 |website=KFOX 14}}</ref>

Jones had a close bond with his father, Alvin Sr., who died on April 6, 2021, from [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bloomquist |first=Bret |date=April 13, 2021 |title=Alvin Jones Sr., father of former UTEP football stars, died of complications from COVID-19 |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/sports/2021/04/13/father-aaron-jones-alvin-sr-died-complications-covid-19/7204674002/ |access-date=September 27, 2021 |website=El Paso Times |language=en-US}}</ref> Jones Sr. was cremated following his death, with the ashes put into a chain for Aaron. During a game against the Detroit Lions, he lost the chain upon scoring a touchdown (one of four that night), but an athletic trainer found it and returned it to him.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2021 |title=NFL Player Aaron Jones Recovers Pendant With Late Father's Ashes After Losing It During A Game |url=https://www.becauseofthemwecan.com/blogs/the-feels/nfl-player-aaron-jones-recovers-pendant-fathers-ashes-losing-during-game |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029182116/https://www.becauseofthemwecan.com/blogs/the-feels/nfl-player-aaron-jones-recovers-pendant-fathers-ashes-losing-during-game |archive-date=October 29, 2021 |access-date=September 27, 2021 |website=BOTWC}}</ref>

Jones was an ambassador of the now bankrupt [[FTX (company)|FTX]] and received compensation via [[cryptocurrency]]. Jones had also purchased an equity stake in the exchange which he is unlikely to recoup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Erazo |first=Felipe |date=September 28, 2021 |title=Crypto Exchange FTX Signs Deal with NFL Player Aaron Jones |url=https://www.financemagnates.com/cryptocurrency/news/crypto-exchange-ftx-signs-deal-with-nfl-player-aaron-jones/ |access-date=October 9, 2022 |website=Finance Magnates}}</ref>

On November 20, 2017, Jones was cited for a traffic stop, an incident that occurred on October 1 in [[Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin]]. The day the incident occurred Jones was speeding at {{convert|79|mph}} at a {{convert|55|mph}} speed limit and had possession of marijuana. Jones was arrested and charged with operating with a restricted controlled substance, operating without a valid license, and speeding.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 20, 2017 |title=Packers RB Aaron Jones facing charges after traffic stop |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/packers-rb-aaron-jones-facing-charges-after-traffic-stop-0ap3000000880287 |access-date=November 20, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Jones pleaded [[no contest]] to the charges and was fined for court costs and had his license suspended for six months.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demovsky |first=Rob |date=February 28, 2018 |title=Packers RB Aaron Jones pleads no contest to marijuana-related charge |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/22608504/packers-rb-aaron-jones-pleads-no-contest-marijuana-related-charge |access-date=September 22, 2020 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

Jones' cousin, [[Tristen Newton]], was the starting point guard for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball]] team during their [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2023 national championship run]] and [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2024 national championship run]], and was named the 2024 [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four Most Outstanding Player]]. 
Aaron and his brother Alvin Jr. attended both Final Fours.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuhagen |first=Christopher |date=April 4, 2023 |title=Packers running back Aaron Jones was a proud cousin and one of the UConn men's basketball team's biggest supporters during its back to back national championship runs |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2023/04/04/packers-running-back-aaron-jones-uconn-basketball-fan-support-cousin-tristen-newton-ncaa-tournament/70078617007/ |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel}}</ref>

'''Aaron Neary''' (born November 15, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (American football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Eastern Washington Eagles football|Eastern Washington Eagles]].

==College career==
Neary attended and played college football at [[Eastern Washington University]].

==Professional career==
===Denver Broncos===
Neary was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] as an undrafted free agent on May 2, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Get to know the Broncos' 21 college free agents|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Get-to-know-the-Broncos-21-college-free-agents/897d0855-5f4e-4e2e-9bb9-9e13300eaf2e|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030141606/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Get-to-know-the-Broncos-21-college-free-agents/897d0855-5f4e-4e2e-9bb9-9e13300eaf2e|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 30, 2017|author=Mason, Andrew|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=May 2, 2016|accessdate=September 4, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 3, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos make 23 moves to pare roster at the deadline|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-make-23-moves-to-pare-roster-at-the-deadline/13177d79-b2fb-44da-b2db-8a604e8e6dec|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819223025/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-make-23-moves-to-pare-roster-at-the-deadline/13177d79-b2fb-44da-b2db-8a604e8e6dec|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 19, 2017|author=Mason, Andrew|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=September 3, 2016|accessdate=September 4, 2017}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On September 5, 2016, Neary was signed to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]' practice squad. He signed a reserve/future contract with the Eagles on January 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eight Signed To Reserve/Future Contracts|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eight-Signed-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/fd99e052-6fd9-4ea0-860d-39f03f975aa5|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180209223815/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eight-Signed-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/fd99e052-6fd9-4ea0-860d-39f03f975aa5|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 9, 2018|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=January 2, 2017|accessdate=September 4, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the team on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles Announce 17 Roster Moves To Get Down To 53 Players|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Announce-17-Roster-Moves-To-Get-Down-To-53-Players/e9f17d13-6a84-4b71-a56e-3806e03a2aa0|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905051907/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Announce-17-Roster-Moves-To-Get-Down-To-53-Players/e9f17d13-6a84-4b71-a56e-3806e03a2aa0|archivedate=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On September 3, 2017, Neary was claimed off waivers by the [[Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Assigned Three Players via Waivers|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Assigned-Three-Players-via-Waivers-/5b84fd28-1e2c-4abb-a853-d1dc1901c417|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007163741/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Assigned-Three-Players-via-Waivers-/5b84fd28-1e2c-4abb-a853-d1dc1901c417|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 7, 2017|author=Simmons, Myles|website=TheRams.com|date=September 3, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the team on September 16, 2017, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Add Donald, Peterson to Active Roster|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Add-Donald-Peterson-to-Active-Roster/43e931d8-a93d-4cb0-8fca-322a00c2ce90|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171119021503/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Add-Donald-Peterson-to-Active-Roster/43e931d8-a93d-4cb0-8fca-322a00c2ce90|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 19, 2017|author=Simmons, Myles|website=TheRams.com|date=September 16, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 27, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams place Marqui Christian on IR|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/12/27/rams-place-marqui-christian-on-ir/|author=Williams, Charean|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=December 27, 2017}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in Week 17 against the San Francisco 49ers, earning the start at center as the Rams rested many of their starters, including starting center [[John Sullivan (center)|John Sullivan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aaron Neary 2017 Stats|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/aaronneary/2556630/gamelogs?season=2017|website=NFL.com|accessdate=February 14, 2018}}</ref>

On August 31, 2018, Neary was waived by the Rams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Continue Friday Cuts|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-continue-friday-cuts|website=TheRams.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On September 2, 2018, Neary was claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns claim 5 players in latest moves to reshaped 53-man roster|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-claim-5-players-in-latest-moves-to-reshaped-53-man-roster|author=Gribble, Andrew|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=September 2, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on September 6, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns claim DL Anthony Zettel|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-claim-dl-anthony-zettel|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=September 6, 2018}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams (second stint)===
On September 11, 2018, Neary was signed to the Los Angeles Rams' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bate |first=Brandon |date=September 11, 2018 |title=Los Angeles Rams bring back Aaron Neary, release OL Jeremiah Kolone |url=https://www.turfshowtimes.com/2018/9/11/17847786/los-angeles-rams-roster-moves-bring-back-aaron-neary-practice-squad |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Turf Show Times|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Rams on February 8, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams sign three players to free agent contracts|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-sign-three-players-to-free-agent-contracts|author=Simmons, Myles|website=TheRams.com|date=February 8, 2019}}</ref>

Neary was suspended the first four games of the 2019 season for a violation of the league's substance abuse policy.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams OL Aaron Neary suspended four games|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/06/28/rams-ol-aaron-neary-suspended-four-games/|author=Alper, Josh|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=June 28, 2019}}</ref> He suffered a broken ankle in the preseason and was ruled out for the year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Josh Carraway tears Achilles; Aaron Neary breaks ankle|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/08/26/josh-carraway-tears-achilles-aaron-neary-breaks-ankle/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 26, 2019}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/suspended list on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |author=Han, Jamie |title=Rams trim roster down to 53 players |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-trim-roster-down-to-53-players |website=TheRams.com |date=August 31, 2019 |accessdate=August 31, 2019}}</ref> He was waived from the reserve/suspended list with an injury settlement on September 10. He was reinstated from suspension by the NFL on October 1, 2019, while still a free agent.

===Chicago Bears===
On November 3, 2020, Neary was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears put Massie on IR; Ifedi, Spriggs on COVID-19 list|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-put-massie-on-ir-ifedi-spriggs-on-covid-19-list|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=November 3, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on November 8 for the team's week 9 game against the [[Tennessee Titans]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite news |author=Alper, Josh |title=Bears put Lachavious Simmons on COVID-19 list |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/11/08/bears-put-lachavious-simmons-on-covid-19-list/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=November 8, 2020 |accessdate=December 13, 2020}}</ref> He was released on November 10.<ref>{{cite news |author=Mayer, Larry |title=Roster Moves: Bears sign OL Kush to practice squad |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-ol-kush-to-practice-squad |website=ChicagoBears.com |date=November 10, 2020 |accessdate=December 16, 2020}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On December 16, 2020, Neary was signed to the [[San Francisco 49ers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-open-practice-window-george-kittle-place-mckivitz-on-covid-19-reserve|website=49ers.com|date=December 16, 2020}}</ref> He was released on January 2, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=49ers Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-activate-compton-sign-kaser-to-practice-squad |website=49ers.com |date=January 2, 2021 |access-date=February 15, 2021}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On September 16, 2018, Neary was arrested for [[misdemeanor]] [[Driving under the influence|DUI]] and [[hit and run]] by the [[Simi Valley Police Department]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/rams/la-sp-aaron-neary-20180917-story.html|title=Rams practice squad member Aaron Neary arrested on suspicion of DUI|last=Klein|first=Gary|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=September 17, 2018 |access-date=September 17, 2018}}</ref>

'''Aaron Fields''' (born January 9, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Atlanta Falcons]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Troy Trojans football|Troy Trojans]].

==Early life==
Fields attended Notasulga High School, where he practiced football and [[basketball]]. He played as a [[wide receiver]], [[tight end]] and [[linebacker]]. He received All-area honors in both sports as a senior.

He accepted a football scholarship from [[Savannah State University]]. He transferred to [[Troy University|Troy State]] after his sophomore season. As a junior, he tallied 7 tackles (one for loss), one sack and 3 quarterback pressures.

As a senior he was named a starter at [[defensive end]], posting 54 tackles (sixth on the team), 7 sacks, 21 quarterback pressures, 14 tackles for loss, 3 passes defensed, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

==Professional career==
===Dallas Cowboys (first stint)===
Fields was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[2000 NFL draft]], on April 19. He was waived on August 27.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/08/28/sports/transactions-879568.html | title=Transactions | newspaper=The New York Times | date=28 August 2000 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On August 30, [[2000 NFL season|2000]], he was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] to their [[practice squad]], where he spent the first 10 weeks of the regular season.

===Dallas Cowboys (second stint)===
On November 8, [[2000 NFL season|2000]], he was signed by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] from the Falcons' [[practice squad]], after [[Chad Hennings]] was lost for the season with a neck injury.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/11/09/sports/transactions-111899.html | title=Transactions | newspaper=The New York Times | date=9 November 2000 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was declared inactive from week 11 to week 13. He saw action against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Washington Redskins]] and [[New York Giants]]. He was deactivated in the season finale. He was released on August 21.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/08/22/sports/transactions-817287.html | title=Transactions | newspaper=The New York Times | date=22 August 2001 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On August 22, [[2001 NFL season|2001]], he was claimed off waivers by the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/08/23/sports/transactions-835757.html | title=Transactions | newspaper=The New York Times | date=23 August 2001 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was cut on August 26.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/08/27/sports/transactions-891789.html | title=Transactions | newspaper=The New York Times | date=27 August 2001 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> On January 24, [[2002 NFL season|2002]], he was re-signed. He was released on August 27.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/08/28/sports/transactions-599760.html | title=Transactions | newspaper=The New York Times | date=28 August 2002 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Edmonton Eskimos===
On April 2, [[2003 CFL season|2003]], he was signed by the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/eskimos-sign-ex-nfl-rush-end/n-1990131 | title=Eskimos sign ex NFL rush end | date=2 April 2003 | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was released on June 6.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/474789408/ | title=Ferrero gets second crack at title vs. Dutch underdog | accessdate=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

'''Aaron Crawford''' (born November 4, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[nose tackle]]. He played [[college football]] at [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]].

==Early life==
Crawford attended [[Stone Bridge High School]] in [[Ashburn, Virginia]]. As a sophomore, he helped his team reach the 2012 Virginia AAA Division 5 title game.<ref name="batten" /> Considered a three-star prospect by 247 Sports, Crawford committed to [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] over offers from [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia]] and [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]].<ref name="martin" /><ref name="batten">{{cite news |last1=Batten |first1=Sammy |title=UNC's Aaron Crawford ready for payback vs. Virginia |url=https://www.newbernsj.com/sports/20191101/uncrsquos-aaron-crawford-ready-for-payback-vs-virginia |access-date=December 3, 2020 |work=[[Sun Journal (New Bern, North Carolina)|Sun Journal]] |date=November 1, 2019 |archive-date=September 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927201916/https://www.newbernsj.com/sports/20191101/uncrsquos-aaron-crawford-ready-for-payback-vs-virginia |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Crawford was sidelined with a knee injury after two games as a true freshman, forcing him to redshirt.<ref name="batten"/> He made 10 starts for North Carolina as a redshirt freshman.<ref name="martin" /> As a sophomore, he started all 12 games and had 29 tackles including 5.0 tackles for loss, 3.0 sacks and a fumble recovery. Crawford tore his PCL and sprained his MCL during preseason camp as a junior. He managed to return on October 13, 2018, but was limited and wore a knee brace, and played his second and final game of the season on October 27. Crawford made one tackle in the two games and called it the toughest part of his career. Coach [[Larry Fedora]] was fired after the season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Alexander |first1=Jonathan |title=A year after he suffered a serious knee injury, UNC's Aaron Crawford wants to dominate |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/unc-now/article233456472.html |access-date=December 3, 2020 |work=[[The News & Observer]] |date=August 3, 2019}}</ref> As a senior in 2019, Crawford started all 13 games and recorded 50 tackles, three sacks, and finished tied for second on the team with 9.0 tackles for loss.<ref name="martin">{{cite news |last1=Martin |first1=Ross |title=Aaron Crawford Signs Free Agent Deal With the Baltimore Ravens |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Aaron-Crawford-Signs-Free-Agent-Deal-With-the-Baltimore-Ravens-NFL-Draft-2020-146477986/ |access-date=December 3, 2020 |work=[[Baltimore Ravens]] |date=April 25, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Baltimore Ravens===
After not being selected in the [[2020 NFL draft]], Crawford signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 25, 2020.<ref name="martin" /> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |author=Mink, Ryan |title=Ravens' Initial 53-Man Roster Is Set |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-initial-53-man-roster-is-set |website=BaltimoreRavens.com |date=September 5, 2020 |access-date=January 10, 2021}}</ref> and signed to their practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Oyefusi |first1=Daniel |title=Ravens finalize 16-man practice squad, including quarterback Tyler Huntley and safety Nigel Warrior |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bs-sp-ravens-practice-squad-quarterback-huntley-warrior-20200906-tkr4jbcf5zco3ch4ktcia3dzwy-story.html |access-date=December 3, 2020 |work=[[Baltimore Sun]] |date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on December 2 for the team's week 12 game against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Shaffer |first1=Jonas |title=Ravens call up 10 players from practice squad vs. Steelers; ailing DT Brandon Williams won't play |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bs-sp-ravens-steelers-roster-20201202-w66uhzc5nvaf3mzhcngltsxsea-story.html |access-date=December 3, 2020 |work=[[Baltimore Sun]] |date=December 2, 2020}}</ref> On January 18, 2021, Crawford signed a reserve/futures contract with the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Future Deals, Waive Four Veterans|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-11-players-to-reserve-future-deals-waive-four-veterans|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=January 18, 2021}}</ref>

On August 31, 2021, Crawford was waived/injured by the Ravens and placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Make Cuts to 53. Here's the Full List|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-make-cuts-to-53-here-s-the-full-list|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref> On March 9, 2022, Crawford re-signed with the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Extend Six Tenders, Including to Quarterback Tyler Huntley|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-extend-exclusive-rights-free-agent-tenders-tyler-huntley|author=Mink, Ryan|website=baltimoreravens.com|date=March 9, 2022}}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, Crawford was waived/injured by the Ravens and placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Make Roster Cuts to 53|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-roster-cuts-53-2022|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref> He was released on September 1.

===New York Giants===
On November 8, 2022, the [[New York Giants]] signed Crawford to their practice squad, but was released the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign DT Aaron Crawford to practice squad; DB Olaijah Griffin released|url=https://www.giants.com/news/aaron-crawford-signed-practice-squad-olaijah-griffin-roster-baltimore-ravens|author=Salomone, Dan|website=Giants.com|date=November 8, 2022}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On December 21, 2022, Crawford was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Christopher Hinton to Active Roster; Place Joe Gaziano on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-sign-christopher-hinton-place-joe-gaziano-injured-reserve|website=Chargers.com|date=December 21, 2022|access-date=December 23, 2022|archive-date=January 29, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129192614/https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-sign-christopher-hinton-place-joe-gaziano-injured-reserve|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Aaron Robinson''' (born November 10, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] and [[UCF Knights football|UCF]], and was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Robinson grew up in [[Deerfield Beach, Florida]], and attended [[Deerfield Beach High School]]. He finished his senior season with 41 tackles, four interceptions and four pass break-ups and was named first-team All-Class 8A. He was a four-star recruit, per [[ESPN]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aaron Robinson - 2020 - Football|url=https://ucfknights.com/sports/football/roster/aaron-robinson/10814|access-date=2022-01-05|website=UCF Athletics|language=en}}</ref> Robinson initially committed to play [[college football]] at Florida before flipping his commitment to Alabama shortly before National Signing Day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 16, 2015 |title=Recruiting: Breaking down Gators' commit, WR/DB Aaron Robinson |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/article/20150616/SPORTS/812032164 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201114207/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/article/20150616/SPORTS/812032164 |archive-date=February 1, 2021 |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[Palm Beach Post]] |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kenyon |first=David |date=February 3, 2016 |title=Aaron Robinson Flips Commitment from Florida to Alabama |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2613515-aaron-robinson-flips-commitment-from-florida-to-alabama |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Robinson began his collegiate career at Alabama. He played in 13 games as a true freshman as a reserve [[cornerback]] and on [[special teams]]. Robinson announced that he intended to transfer from [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] during the summer before his sophomore year and ultimately chose to enroll at [[University of Central Florida|UCF]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 20, 2017 |title=Alabama players B.J. Emmons, Aaron Robinson plan to transfer |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/news/20170720/alabama-players-bj-emmons-aaron-robinson-plan-to-transfer |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[The Tuscaloosa News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 29, 2017 |title=Alabama CB Aaron Robinson transferring to UCF |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-recruiting/os-sp-ucf-aaron-robinson-transfer-alabama-20170729-story.html |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref>

Robinson sat out his first year with the [[UCF Knights football|Knights]] per [[NCAA]] transfer rules.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2018 |title=UCF defensive back Aaron Robinson savors return to field |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/ucf-knights/os-sp-ucf-football-news-1010-story.html |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> He suffered a serious injury on the opening kickoff of his first game with the team and missed multiple weeks of his [[redshirted|redshirt]] sophomore season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2018 |title=UCF's Aaron Robinson stretchered off field after season-opening kickoff |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2018/08/30/ucfs-aaron-robinson-carted-off-field-after-season-opening-kickoff/1151040002/ |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> As a redshirt junior, Robinson recorded 54 tackles, 5.5 tackles for loss, three interceptions and 10 pass breakups with one forced fumble and was named second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murschel |first=Matt |date=July 21, 2020 |title=UCF DB Richie Grant, Aaron Robinson named to Jim Thorpe Award watch list |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/ucf-knights/os-sp-ucf-football-thorpe-award-watch-list-20200720-ghnkfswnpndv3ftanpenwqkz7q-story.html |access-date=January 27, 2021 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]]}}</ref> Robinson was named second-team All-AAC again as a redshirt senior.

Robinson was placed on the reserve/PUP list to start the 2023 season as he recovered from his knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants announce 53-man roster for 2023|url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-roster-2023-nfl-season-joe-schoen-brian-daboll-transactions|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref>

Robinson was waived by the Giants on July 31, 2024 following a failed physical.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elsen |first=Michael |date=31 July 2024 |title=Giants sign OL Greg Van Roten; CB Aaron Robinson waived/failed physical |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-offensive-lineman-greg-van-roten-las-vegas-raiders-carmen-bricillo-aaron-robinson |access-date=1 August 2024 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

'''Aaron Patrick''' (born December 21, 1996) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive lineman]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels football|Eastern Kentucky]].

==College career==
Patrick was a member of the [[Eastern Kentucky Colonels football|Eastern Kentucky Colonels]] for five seasons. Patrick finished his collegiate career with 27.5 sacks, which are the second-most in school history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.richmondregister.com/sports/patrick-picks-up-another-prestigious-postseason-honor/article_c4bc85d7-7dfa-546b-9e74-532709164cba.html|title=Patrick picks up another prestigious postseason honor|work=[[Richmond Register]]|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=November 15, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Patrick was signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] to their practice squad on December 14, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/14/jags-sign-te-bug-howard-de-aaron-patrick-along-with-other-transactions/|title=Jags sign TE Bug Howard, DE Aaron Patrick along with other transactions|first=James|last=Johnson|website=Jaguars Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=December 14, 2020|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref> He signed a reserve/futures contract with the team on January 4, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-11-players-to-reserve-future-contracts|title=Jaguars Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts|website=Jaguars.com|date=January 4, 2021|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref> Patrick was waived on August 31, 2021, during final roster cuts but was resigned to the team's practice squad on September 9.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2021/09/09/jaguars-add-edge-rusher-aaron-patrick-to-practice-squad-release-k-kaare-vedvik/|title=Jaguars add edge rusher Aaron Patrick to practice squad, release K Kaare Vedvik|first=Tyler|last=Nettuno|website=Jaguars Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=September 9, 2021|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
The [[Denver Broncos]] signed Patrick to their active roster off of the Jaguars practice squad on September 23, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/nfl-sports-jacksonville-jaguars-denver-broncos-nate-mccrary-92655763a86bc193b1f7fb567d789940|title=Broncos sign OLB Aaron Patrick off Jags’ practice squad|website=[[Associated Press|APNews.com]]|date=September 23, 2021|access-date=October 4, 2021}}</ref>

In Week 6 of the 2022 season, Patrick suffered a [[torn ACL]] and was placed on injured reserve on October 21, 2022. The injury came after Patrick was forced out of bounds and collided with a league official. As he did so, his foot planted on a fabric mat used to cover broadcast cords and cables, and caused his knee to bend awkwardly.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos LB Aaron Patrick has torn ACL, out for season|url=https://www.milehighreport.com/2022/10/18/23411347/broncos-aaron-patrick-injury|work=Mile High Report|date=October 18, 2022}}</ref> On November 17, Patrick launched a lawsuit against the NFL for "unspecified damages, including lost bonuses and future earning potential".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Broncos OLB Aaron Patrick Launches Lawsuit over ACL Injury|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-aaron-patrick-lawsuit-nfl-chargers-injury|access-date=July 31, 2023|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

On August 29, 2023, Patrick was waived by the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos make series of transactions to reduce active roster to league-mandated limit|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-transactions-to-reduce-active-roster-to-league-mandated-l|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders===
On April 4, 2025, it was announced that Patrick had signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.riderville.com/2025/04/04/roughriders-add-all-american-pass-rusher-aaron-patrick/ |title=Roughriders add All-American pass rusher Aaron Patrick |website=Jaguars Wire|publisher=[[Saskatchewan Roughriders]]|date=April 4, 2025}}</ref>

On May 10, Patrick retired from professional football.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Dave |title=Former MAC player of the year Peny Boone among first Saskatchewan Roughriders roster cuts |url=https://www.sportscage.com/roughriders/training-camp/former-mac-player-of-the-year-peny-boone-among-first-saskatchewan-roughriders-roster-cuts-12261632 |website=SportsCage.com |access-date=11 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Aaron Joseph Monteiro''' (born March 25, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Columbus Aviators]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]] and has been a member of the [[Miami Dolphins]], [[New England Patriots]], [[Carolina Panthers]], and [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

== College career ==
Monteiro was ranked as a three–star [[College recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com]] coming out of high school.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Monteiro, Boston College Eagles, Offensive Tackle |url=https://247sports.com/player/aaron-monteiro-55086/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=247Sports }}</ref> He committed to [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]] on March 29, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Monteiro, Brockton, Offensive Tackle |url=https://247sports.com/player/aaron-monteiro-55086/high-school-94611/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=247Sports }}</ref> He made the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] third-team in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Monteiro - Football |url=https://bceagles.com/sports/football/roster/aaron-monteiro/10186 |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=Boston College Athletics }}</ref>

=== Miami Dolphins ===
After going undrafted in the [[2019 NFL draft]], Monteiro signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] on May 10, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hier |first=Justin |date=2019-05-10 |title=Dolphins announce official list of undrafted free agent signees; 18 UDFA rookies to join the team |url=https://www.thephinsider.com/2019/5/10/18563764/miami-dolphins-announce-official-list-of-undrafted-free-agent-signees-18-udfa-rookies-to-join-team |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=The Phinsider }}</ref> He was released on August 21.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2019-08-31 |title=Dolphins Officially Cut 32 Players |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/dolphins-roster-cuts/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref>

=== New England Patriots ===
On October 22, 2019, the [[New England Patriots]] signed Monteiro to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Official New England Patriots News and Analysis |url=https://www.patriots.com/team/transactions/2019 |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=www.patriots.com }}</ref> He was released on October 29.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Patriots release K Mike Nugent and TE Eric Tomlinson; Release OL Aaron Monteiro from practice squad |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-release-k-mike-nugent-and-te-eric-tomlinson-release-ol-aaron-monteiro-f |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=www.patriots.com }}</ref>

=== Carolina Panthers ===
On November 12, 2019, the [[Carolina Panthers]] signed Monteiro to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2019-11-12 |title=Panthers Sign DB Corn Elder Off Giants' PS, Add Two |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-sign-db-corn-elder-off-giants-ps-add-two/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was signed to a future deal on December 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=2019-12-30 |title=Panthers Sign Nine Players To Futures Deals |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-sign-nine-players-to-futures-deals/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was released on September 5, 2020, but was re-signed to the practice squad on September 21.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-09-05 |title=Carolina Panthers 2020 roster cuts tracker |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2020/09/05/carolina-panthers-2020-roster-cuts-tracker/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=Panthers Wire }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2020-09-21 |title=Panthers Release K Kai Forbath From PS, Re-Sign OL Aaron Monteiro |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-release-k-kai-forbath-from-ps-re-sign-ol-aaron-monteiro/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 19, 2020, and once again on January 2, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Comeaux |first=Jonathan |date=2021-01-02 |title=Panthers Promote Three Including QB Tommy Stevens |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-promote-three-including-qb-tommy-stevens/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was signed to a future deal on January 4, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2021-01-04 |title=Panthers Sign TE Colin Thompson To Extension, Sign 14 To Futures Deals |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-sign-te-colin-thompson-to-extension-sign-14-to-futures-deals/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> 

On August 30, 2021, Monteiro was released by the Panthers but was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-27 |title=Carolina Panthers make cuts, unveil initial 53-man roster |url=https://abc11.com/post/nfl-2024-roster-cuts-carolina-panthers-prepare-roster-cuts-nfl-deadline-looms/15234738/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=ABC11 Raleigh-Durham }}</ref> He was released on November 3, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ulrich |first=Logan |date=2021-11-03 |title=Panthers Designate RB Christian McCaffrey & P Joseph Charlton To Return From IR, Make Two PS Moves |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-designate-rb-christian-mccaffrey-p-joseph-charlton-to-return-from-ir-make-two-ps-moves/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on November 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=2021-11-09 |title=Panthers Release QB Josh Love From PS, Re-Sign OL Aaron Monterio |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/panthers-release-qb-josh-love-from-ps-re-sign-ol-aaron-monterio/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was released on May 12, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-12 |title=Panthers release two players to get to 90-man roster limit |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/panthers-release-two-players-90-205323297.html |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=Yahoo Sports }}</ref>

=== Washington Commanders ===
On May 23, 2022, Monteiro was signed by the [[Washington Commanders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Commanders sign T Aaron Monteiro |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/washington-commanders-sign-aaron-monteiro |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=www.commanders.com }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bill-in-Bangkok |date=2022-05-24 |title=Who is Aaron Monteiro, the free agent tackle signed by the Commanders this week? |url=https://www.hogshaven.com/2022/5/24/23139265/who-is-aaron-monteiro-the-free-agent-tackle-signed-by-the-commanders-this-week |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=Hogs Haven |language=en}}</ref> He was released on August 30, 2022, but was re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Grindley |first=Wyatt |date=2022-08-31 |title=Commanders Sign 15 Players To Practice Squad |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/commanders-sign-15-players-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co }}</ref> He was released on August 28, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Football Team Trades & Signings {{!}} Washington Football Team - WashingtonFootball.com |url=https://www.commanders.com/team/transactions/2023 |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=www.commanders.com }}</ref>

=== San Antonio Brahmas ===
On December 13, 2023, Monteiro signed with the [[San Antonio Brahmas]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=UFL Transactions |url=https://uflboard.com/ufl-transactions/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=UFLBoard.com }}</ref>

On January 13, 2026, Monteiro was selected by the [[Columbus Aviators]] in the [[2026 UFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theufl.com/news/2026-ufl-draft-day-one|title=2026 UFL Draft: Day One|website=theufl.com|date=January 13, 2026|access-date=January 16, 2026}}</ref>
